**4. [CheXpert Plus](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus)** covers 64,725 Stanford patients, so it gives you a second large site for cross-hospital evaluation.
- **Contents:** each report is split into 11 sections; images come as DICOM and PNG.
- **Steps:** the page's "Download here" link goes to Redivis. Creating an account and accepting Stanford's terms there is from memory.
- **Licence conflict:** the Stanford portal's own record names the "Open Use of Data Agreement v1.0", which permits redistribution. The paper and other sources say the Stanford Research Use Agreement, which is non-commercial with no redistribution. Assume non-commercial until you see the terms at download.
- **Size:** 3.46 TB in total. A third party reports a Redivis export cap of 100 GB per 30 days, which I could not verify.

**5. [Interpret-CXR](https://huggingface.co/datasets/StanfordAIMI/rrg24-shared-task-bionlp)** is a ready-made Findings/Impression training set from the RRG24 shared task.
- **Contents:** sections drawn from CheXpert, PadChest, BIMCV-COVID19 and Open-i, plus a script to add MIMIC-CXR once you hold that credential.
- **Steps:** submit your Hugging Face details and a CITI training verification link, then wait for owner approval.
- **Limits:** the PadChest and BIMCV text is GPT-4 translation from Spanish, not what the radiologist wrote.

**6. [PadChest](https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/)** is the largest non-English option, from Hospital San Juan in Alicante.
- **Steps:** read the [research use agreement](https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/padchest-dataset-research-use-agreement/), then fill in the Google Form behind "Descargar Dataset completo". The page does not say whether requests are reviewed.
- **Limits:** the paper describes the `Report` field as "a text snippet extracted from the original report", so it is an excerpt. From memory it is also lower-cased with punctuation stripped; look at the 167 MB Kaggle sample linked on the page before committing.
- **Conditions:** research only; do not pass the link outside your organisation.

**7. [CASIA-CXR](https://www.casia-cxr.net/)** has reports written natively in French and was built for report generation, with published baselines.
- **Steps:** submit the request form with an institutional email and a project description, then sign the agreement the authors send. An 80 MB sample downloads freely.
- **Conditions:** the agreement forbids translating the reports into other languages without written permission, which rules out translate-then-train. No redistribution.

**8. [PadChest-GR](https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest-gr/)** is a bilingual evaluation set with radiologist-drawn boxes.
- **Limits:** the 10,459 one-finding sentences were produced by GPT-4 extraction and translation, then checked by radiologists, so they are not the original prose.
- **Steps:** same form and agreement as PadChest.

**9. [BIMCV-COVID19+](https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/bimcv-covid19/)** is a second Spanish source from the Valencia region.
- **Contents:** the page confirms radiology reports are included; that they are Spanish free text is from memory.
- **Limits:** all patients are COVID-19 positive, so the mix of findings is skewed. It also holds 7,918 CT studies to filter out.
- **Steps:** Google Form for "Iteration 1+2+3".

**10. [REFLACX](https://physionet.org/content/reflacx-xray-localization/1.0.0/)** has reports freshly dictated by radiologists for MIMIC-CXR frontal images, with eye tracking. It is useful as second-reader references, but the images still need the MIMIC credential.

**Papers that used these:**
- MIMIC-CXR: [describing paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-019-0322-0); [cross-domain audit with IU X-Ray](https://doi.org/10.2196/95888).
- ReXGradient-160K: [describing paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.00228).
- IU X-Ray: [describing paper](https://scholarworks.indianapolis.iu.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/9ab6a7d1-790f-4fc1-85b9-18afeb0d0c3f/content).
- CheXpert Plus: [describing paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.19538); [LLaVA-Rad](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58344-x); [AAAI 2026 report generation](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40688).
- Interpret-CXR: [RRG24 system paper](https://aclanthology.org/2024.bionlp-1.51.pdf).
- PadChest: [describing paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1901.07441v2). PadChest-GR: [NEJM AI](https://doi.org/10.1056/aidbp2401120).
- CASIA-CXR: [Neurocomputing 2024](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925231224012499).

## Known, not confirmed
- **CheXpert Plus:** the dataset and its contents are confirmed from Stanford's pages. The current download steps and governing licence are not; check the Redivis page.
- **Open-i:** the files are confirmed downloadable. The licence wording is second-hand.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[CANDID-PTX](https://auckland.figshare.com/articles/dataset/CANDID-PTX/14173982) and CANDID** (New Zealand, 19k and 53k radiographs with reports): the CANDID-PTX record states that since Feb 2024 it "is not available for access by users outside Health New Zealand". The larger CANDID record could not be read; whether it is closed too is my assumption.
- **[BRAX](https://physionet.org/content/brax/1.1.0/)**: labels derived from Portuguese reports, but the report text is not released (from memory).
- **CheXpert (original), NIH ChestX-ray14, VinDr-CXR**: images and labels only.
- **CX-CHR, CH-Xray (Chinese)**: used in papers but not publicly released, per search results.
- **Kaggle, Hugging Face or torrent copies** of IU X-Ray, MIMIC-CXR or PadChest: unofficial mirrors; the original terms still apply.

## What I could not find
- No public chest X-ray set with native German, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Italian, Russian, Vietnamese or Chinese report text that an outsider can obtain.
- I did not check MIDRC or Emory CXR.
- One paper index was down, so the evidence-of-use list is thinner than it could be.

## Next step
Download IU X-Ray and accept the ReXGradient-160K terms today, and start the PhysioNet credentialing now, since its training certificate also serves the Interpret-CXR request. For the secondary experiment, send the PadChest form and the CASIA-CXR request in parallel, because neither states a turnaround.

The interactive version, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-0kxBml/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-mimic-cxr
graders.evidence:
The datasets below include actual report text. I'm working from memory rather than checking the hosting pages, so confirm sizes and licence terms before you commit.

## English

| Dataset | Size | Report text | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MIMIC-CXR** (Beth Israel Deaconess, Boston) | ~377k images, ~228k studies, ~65k patients | Full de-identified reports, with findings and impression sections in most | PhysioNet credentialed access (steps below) |
| **CheXpert Plus** (Stanford) | ~223k image–report pairs, ~188k studies, ~65k patients | De-identified reports split into sections | Stanford AIMI portal: sign in, accept the research use agreement, download with azcopy |
| **ReXGradient-160K** (Rad AI / Harvard) | ~160k studies, ~273k images, ~109k patients across several US health systems | Findings and impression | Gated on Hugging Face: accept the licence on the dataset page (non-commercial, as I recall) |
| **IU X-Ray / Open-i** (Indiana University) | 7,470 images, 3,955 reports | Findings and impression, with over-aggressive de-identification (`XXXX` tokens) | Open download from NLM Open-i, no registration or agreement |
| **CANDID-PTX** (Dunedin, New Zealand) | ~19k radiographs | De-identified reports, skewed towards pneumothorax, chest tubes and rib fractures | Data use agreement plus a short online ethics course, via University of Otago |

MIMIC-CXR is the standard benchmark, and getting it involves:

1. Create a PhysioNet account and apply for credentialing, which asks for a reference such as a supervisor.
2. Complete the CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" course.
3. Sign the data use agreement on the project page.

Approval typically takes days to a couple of weeks. The reports are in the base MIMIC-CXR project; MIMIC-CXR-JPG adds JPGs (~560 GB instead of ~4.7 TB of DICOMs) and the official train/val/test split. The agreement forbids sharing the data with third parties, which includes sending reports to ordinary hosted LLM APIs.

For CheXpert Plus, the PNG version is a few hundred GB and the DICOMs run to terabytes. The original CheXpert release has labels only, so you need the Plus version.

## Non-English

- **PadChest (Spanish):** ~160k images from ~110k studies and ~67k patients in Alicante. You submit a request form on the BIMCV site and accept the research use agreement; the full set is about 1 TB. The released report text is preprocessed (lowercased, punctuation stripped, as I recall), so it is not pristine prose.
- **PadChest-GR (Spanish and English):** ~4.5k studies with sentence-level findings and bounding boxes, through the same BIMCV request route. The sentences were rewritten by radiologists for grounding and are not the original reports.
- **BIMCV-COVID19 (Spanish):** a few thousand COVID-era studies mixing chest X-ray and CT, with reports. It is downloadable from BIMCV with lighter terms than PadChest.
- **CASIA-CXR (French):** ~11k frontal radiographs with French reports, published in 2024. I'm least sure of this one's access details, so check the paper.
- **CX-CHR (Chinese):** appears in many papers but was never publicly released; you would have to ask the authors.

## Labels only

NIH ChestX-ray14, the original CheXpert, VinDr-CXR and BRAX provide only labels, though they are often listed alongside the datasets above.

## Recommendation

Start the MIMIC-CXR credentialing now, since it is the only step with a waiting period, and build your pipeline on IU X-Ray in the meantime. Use CheXpert Plus or ReXGradient for cross-institution evaluation, and PadChest for the non-English experiment.

cases.name: ho-h-derm-skin-tone
cases.promptMarkdown: For a fairness audit I want to test whether dermatology image classifiers do worse on darker skin. graders.name: 01-recall-fitzpatrick17k
graders.evidence:
Five public datasets have both a skin tone label and a diagnosis with real numbers in types V and VI; none is ideal alone, so a credible audit will combine two or three. All facts below were checked on 2026-11-12, and the V/VI counts marked "counted" are ones I tallied from each dataset's own metadata file.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** a Fitzpatrick or Monk label per image or patient.
- **R2 (must):** a diagnosis per image or patient.
- **R3 (must):** types V and VI in the hundreds.
- **R4 (nice to have, my assumption):** lighter types in the same dataset, so the comparison isn't confounded by different sources.
- **R5:** clinical photos or dermoscopy, any condition.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | V / VI | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fitzpatrick17k | Labels: direct download. Images: fetch by URL, or request form | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 | 16,577 images, 114 conditions | 1,533 / 635 (counted) | Strong | today |
| 2 | DermaCon-IN | Direct download | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 5,450 images, 3,002 patients, 245 conditions | 1,285 / 136 (counted) | Strong, but no types I–II | today |
| 3 | SCIN | Direct download | Custom SCIN Data Use License | 5,033 cases, 10,000+ images | 229 / 27 among 3,061 cases with a diagnosis (counted) | Partial | today |
| 4 | DDI | Free registration and research use agreement | Stanford agreement, non-commercial | 656 images, 570 patients | 207 in V–VI combined | Partial (small) | today |
| 5 | PASSION | Request form, likely days | Custom, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | 341 / 88 in the 986-image test split | Partial | today |
| 6 | MILK10k | Direct download | CC BY-NC 4.0 | 5,240 lesions, 10,480 images | 111 lesions in its two darkest classes (counted) | Weak | today |

## Details

**1. [Fitzpatrick17k](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)**
- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, with all six types (I 2,947; II 4,808; III 3,308; IV 2,781; V 1,533; VI 635; 565 unlabelled).
- **Why it fits:** it has the largest V–VI count and light types in the same set.
- **Weakness:** diagnoses are atlas captions and skin types come from non-dermatologist annotators; duplicates and mislabels are documented. Evaluate on a cleaned version such as [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick).
- **Access:** the label CSV is in the repo; images come from the URLs in the CSV (some are dead) or via the authors' form.
- **Used by:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201), [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13), [quality audit 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04382-5).

**2. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient photos from South India with dermatologist diagnoses, plus Fitzpatrick and Monk labels on every image.
- **Counts:** Fitzpatrick III 1,403; IV 2,620; V 1,285; VI 136. Monk 7–9 covers 2,059 images. The V–VI images come from 993 patients.
- **Weakness:** there are no type I–II images, and only 52 images are neoplasms; most are infectious or inflammatory.
- **Access:** download two zips (about 3.6 GB) and the metadata table from Harvard Dataverse.
- **Used by:** [describing paper](https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-3742).

**3. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced US smartphone photos with three tone labels per case: self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk.
- **Counts:** over all cases, the dermatologist estimate gives V 359 and VI 69. Only 3,061 cases have a condition label, which cuts this to 229 and 27.
- **Weakness:** the diagnosis is a weighted differential from photos, not a confirmed one. Self-reported and estimated type VI disagree (143 vs 69).
- **Access:** public Google Cloud bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not confirm the licence's commercial-use terms.

**4. [DDI](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions from Stanford, with 208 type I–II images matched to 207 type V–VI on diagnosis category, age, sex and date.
- **Why it fits:** it has the best label quality here and is built for exactly this audit.
- **Weakness:** it is small, and tone is given in three bins, so V and VI are not separable.
- **Access:** register individually on the Stanford AIMI portal and accept the agreement. No redistribution or sharing the link, and each team member registers separately.
- **Used by:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**5. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** mostly paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, Fitzpatrick III–VI only.
- **Labels:** eczema, fungal, scabies, other, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Weakness:** there are no light types, and whole-dataset tone counts are not published; I only found the test split in the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04584).
- **Access:** Google Form request; approval time is not stated. Non-commercial, no reposting.

**6. [MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq)**
- **Contents:** paired clinical and dermoscopic images, 95.7% biopsy-confirmed. It is the only dermoscopy option with a tone label.
- **Weakness:** the tone scale is its own (0 very dark to 5 very light, deliberately not Fitzpatrick), and classes 0–1 hold only 6 and 105 lesions.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** the DOI resolves to Stanford Redivis; it covers self-identified Asian patients. I could not read the page or the paper, so tone labels and access terms are unconfirmed.
- **[Black skin lesions, UNICAMP](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions assessed on the Fitzpatrick scale, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted and need a request from an institutional email; size and V/VI counts are unconfirmed.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://doi.org/10.34970/962049):** CC BY 4.0, with Monk, Pantone and colorimeter tone measurements. I did not confirm whether diagnoses are included or how many dark-skin cases it has.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** has a Fitzpatrick column but only about 10 type V and 1 type VI images (from a [secondary source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13459198/), not counted by me).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://doi.org/10.71718/15nz-jv40):** Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **HAM10000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt, DermNet:** no skin tone label (from memory, not rechecked).
- **SkinCon, SkinCAP, FitzDerm-CF:** extra annotations on Fitzpatrick17k and DDI images, not new patients.
- **[Synthetic dermatology dataset on Mendeley](https://doi.org/10.17632/bb844rcjx5.1):** synthetic images are not audit evidence.

## What I could not find
- A dermoscopy dataset with Fitzpatrick labels and hundreds of V–VI lesions.
- A single dataset with confirmed diagnoses, all six types and more than about 200 V–VI images.
- Search coverage has small holes: Zenodo rate-limited one of six queries, and Stanford Redivis pages were unreadable.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k (cleaned) and SCIN for six-type comparisons, and register for DDI as the high-quality check. Add DermaCon-IN for volume in type V, and send the PASSION request now if your classifier covers common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Type VI is the thin spot everywhere (635, 136, 27, 88), so report V and VI separately where the data allows.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-2tfNLK/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

| 2 | DermaCon-IN | Direct download | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 5,450 images, 3,002 patients, 245 conditions | 1,285 / 136 (counted) | Strong, but no types I–II | today |

| 4 | DDI | Free registration and research use agreement | Stanford agreement, non-commercial | 656 images, 570 patients | 207 in V–VI combined | Partial (small) | today |
| 5 | PASSION | Request form, likely days | Custom, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | 341 / 88 in the 986-image test split | Partial | today |
| 6 | MILK10k | Direct download | CC BY-NC 4.0 | 5,240 lesions, 10,480 images | 111 lesions in its two darkest classes (counted) | Weak | today |

## Details

**1. [Fitzpatrick17k](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)**
- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, with all six types (I 2,947; II 4,808; III 3,308; IV 2,781; V 1,533; VI 635; 565 unlabelled).
- **Why it fits:** it has the largest V–VI count and light types in the same set.
- **Weakness:** diagnoses are atlas captions and skin types come from non-dermatologist annotators; duplicates and mislabels are documented. Evaluate on a cleaned version such as [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick).
- **Access:** the label CSV is in the repo; images come from the URLs in the CSV (some are dead) or via the authors' form.
- **Used by:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201), [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13), [quality audit 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04382-5).

**2. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient photos from South India with dermatologist diagnoses, plus Fitzpatrick and Monk labels on every image.
- **Counts:** Fitzpatrick III 1,403; IV 2,620; V 1,285; VI 136. Monk 7–9 covers 2,059 images. The V–VI images come from 993 patients.
- **Weakness:** there are no type I–II images, and only 52 images are neoplasms; most are infectious or inflammatory.
- **Access:** download two zips (about 3.6 GB) and the metadata table from Harvard Dataverse.
- **Used by:** [describing paper](https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-3742).

**3. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced US smartphone photos with three tone labels per case: self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk.
- **Counts:** over all cases, the dermatologist estimate gives V 359 and VI 69. Only 3,061 cases have a condition label, which cuts this to 229 and 27.
- **Weakness:** the diagnosis is a weighted differential from photos, not a confirmed one. Self-reported and estimated type VI disagree (143 vs 69).
- **Access:** public Google Cloud bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not confirm the licence's commercial-use terms.

**4. [DDI](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions from Stanford, with 208 type I–II images matched to 207 type V–VI on diagnosis category, age, sex and date.
- **Why it fits:** it has the best label quality here and is built for exactly this audit.
- **Weakness:** it is small, and tone is given in three bins, so V and VI are not separable.
- **Access:** register individually on the Stanford AIMI portal and accept the agreement. No redistribution or sharing the link, and each team member registers separately.
- **Used by:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**5. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** mostly paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, Fitzpatrick III–VI only.
- **Labels:** eczema, fungal, scabies, other, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Weakness:** there are no light types, and whole-dataset tone counts are not published; I only found the test split in the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04584).
- **Access:** Google Form request; approval time is not stated. Non-commercial, no reposting.

**6. [MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq)**
- **Contents:** paired clinical and dermoscopic images, 95.7% biopsy-confirmed. It is the only dermoscopy option with a tone label.
- **Weakness:** the tone scale is its own (0 very dark to 5 very light, deliberately not Fitzpatrick), and classes 0–1 hold only 6 and 105 lesions.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** the DOI resolves to Stanford Redivis; it covers self-identified Asian patients. I could not read the page or the paper, so tone labels and access terms are unconfirmed.
- **[Black skin lesions, UNICAMP](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions assessed on the Fitzpatrick scale, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted and need a request from an institutional email; size and V/VI counts are unconfirmed.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://doi.org/10.34970/962049):** CC BY 4.0, with Monk, Pantone and colorimeter tone measurements. I did not confirm whether diagnoses are included or how many dark-skin cases it has.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** has a Fitzpatrick column but only about 10 type V and 1 type VI images (from a [secondary source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13459198/), not counted by me).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://doi.org/10.71718/15nz-jv40):** Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **HAM10000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt, DermNet:** no skin tone label (from memory, not rechecked).
- **SkinCon, SkinCAP, FitzDerm-CF:** extra annotations on Fitzpatrick17k and DDI images, not new patients.
- **[Synthetic dermatology dataset on Mendeley](https://doi.org/10.17632/bb844rcjx5.1):** synthetic images are not audit evidence.

## What I could not find
- A dermoscopy dataset with Fitzpatrick labels and hundreds of V–VI lesions.
- A single dataset with confirmed diagnoses, all six types and more than about 200 V–VI images.
- Search coverage has small holes: Zenodo rate-limited one of six queries, and Stanford Redivis pages were unreadable.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k (cleaned) and SCIN for six-type comparisons, and register for DDI as the high-quality check. Add DermaCon-IN for volume in type V, and send the PASSION request now if your classifier covers common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Type VI is the thin spot everywhere (635, 136, 27, 88), so report V and VI separately where the data allows.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-2tfNLK/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-fitzpatrick17k
graders.evidence:
Five public datasets meet your criteria to a useful degree; three fit well (Fitzpatrick17k, DDI, PASSION) and two fit partly (SCIN, DermaCon-IN). None is both large and biopsy-confirmed in types V and VI, so plan on combining two or three.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** a Fitzpatrick or Monk label for every image or patient.
- **R2 (must):** a diagnosis for every image.
- **R3 (must):** types V and VI in the hundreds, not a handful.
- **R4 (nice to have):** obtainable by an outside researcher, sooner is better. I assumed non-commercial research use is acceptable, since nearly all of these forbid commercial use.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Dark-skin representation | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fitzpatrick17k | Labels download directly; images via source links or a form to the maintainers | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 | 16,577 clinical images, 114 conditions | V: 1,533; VI: 635 | Strong | Today (I counted the label file) |
| 2 | DDI (Stanford) | Free registration plus research-use agreement | Stanford agreement, non-commercial | 656 images, 570 patients, biopsy-proven | V–VI: 207 | Strong | Today (counts from the paper) |
| 3 | PASSION | Request form, owner approval, probably days | PASSION licence, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | Test split of 986: V: 341; VI: 88 | Strong | Today |
| 4 | SCIN (Google) | Direct download | Custom SCIN Data Use License | 10,408 images, 5,033 cases | Dermatologist-estimated V: 359; VI: 69 | Partial | Today (I counted the label files) |
| 5 | DermaCon-IN | Listed as open on Harvard Dataverse; the paper mentions a verification step | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 5,450 images, 3,002 patients, 245 diagnoses | IV and V most common; VI: 136 | Partial | Partly; page not readable today |

## Details

**1. [Fitzpatrick17k](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)**
- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, each with a Fitzpatrick label; 565 images are unlabelled.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set with V and VI in the high hundreds each, reported separately.
- **Weaknesses:** skin type was judged from the photo by crowd annotators, diagnoses are atlas labels and not biopsy-confirmed, and label noise and duplicates are known. [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick) provides cleaning annotations.
- **Access:** download `fitzpatrick17k.csv`, then fetch images from its `url` column (some links are dead) or use the form in the README to ask for the full image set.
- **Used in:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201) and [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13).

**2. [DDI, Diverse Dermatology Images](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions; the V–VI images (159 benign, 48 malignant) are matched to I–II images on diagnosis category, age, gender and date.
- **Why it fits:** it was designed for exactly this audit, and it has the best ground truth.
- **Weaknesses:** it is small. From memory, skin tone is recorded as pairs (I–II, III–IV, V–VI), so V and VI cannot be separated.
- **Access:** register individually and accept the agreement ("personal, non-commercial research purposes only"). A copy is also listed on [Stanford Redivis](https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/3r16-5mby7gfer).
- **Used in:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**3. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, covering eczema, fungal infections, scabies and other conditions, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set collected in sub-Saharan Africa, with about 43% V–VI in the test split.
- **Weaknesses:** there are no type I–II images, so it gives no light-versus-dark contrast by itself. It has no skin cancer, and the paper does not publish full-set counts per type.
- **Access:** fill in the Google Form on the project page; the download link may not be shared.
- **Used in:** [Gottfrois et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72384-1_66).

**4. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced phone photos from US internet users, with self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk scale from two rater pools.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only open set with Monk labels and both self-reported and estimated tone.
- **Weaknesses:**
  - Tone labels are incomplete: the dermatologist estimate is missing for 731 cases and self-report is missing or unassigned for 2,858.
  - Dark tones are thin: self-report gives V: 214 and VI: 143, and only 207 cases are Monk 7–10 by the US raters.
  - Diagnoses are differential lists made from the photos, and only 3,049 cases were judged gradable.
- **Access:** follow `scin_demo.ipynb`, or fetch the files from the public bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not read the licence's commercial-use terms.
- **Used in:** [one classification paper](https://doi.org/10.5267/j.ijdns.2024.11.003).

**5. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient clinical photos from South India with a diagnosis hierarchy, each labelled on both the Fitzpatrick and Monk scales by trained raters.
- **Why it fits:** it has complete dual-scale labels and many type IV–V images.
- **Weaknesses:** type VI is 136 images, the exact type V count is not in the paper text, and there are few I–II images.
- **Access:** open the Dataverse record in a browser. The registry lists it as open, but the paper says access "will be granted following a background verification process".
- **Paper:** [arXiv 2506.06099](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06099).

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** Stanford's follow-up set of self-identified Asian patients. The record exists, but I could not read its contents or terms because the page renders by JavaScript. It is unlikely to add many V–VI images.
- **[Black skin lesions set, University of Campinas](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions (palms, soles, nails) on Black skin, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted behind a request from an institutional email. Whether each image carries a skin tone label, and how many images there are, is not stated.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq):** has a six-level skin tone label per lesion, but the darkest levels are reportedly under 1% of 5,240 lesions (unofficial source, I did not count it).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/mra-midas-Multimodal-Image-Dataset-for-AI-based-Skin-Cancer):** Fitzpatrick per patient and biopsy-proven, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** open with a Fitzpatrick field, but from memory it is filled for only part of the images and V–VI are a handful.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://api.isic-archive.com/collections/413/):** 4,879 dermoscopic images balanced across all six types with Monk and colorimeter readings, but every lesion is assumed benign. It is usable only for a false-positive check.
- **HAM10000, BCN20000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt:** no skin tone labels (from memory).
- **[electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR](https://huggingface.co/datasets/electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR):** appears to attach African metadata to existing HAM10000/ISIC image IDs, so it is probably synthetic.

## What I could not find
- A public dermoscopy dataset with hundreds of confirmed type V–VI malignant lesions; DDI's 48 malignant V–VI images are the best available.
- Monk-scale labels outside SCIN, DermaCon-IN and the benign-only MSKCC set.

I searched five registries, the literature and the web; Harvard Dataverse and medRxiv refused automated requests.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k for statistical power and SCIN for Monk labels, register for DDI as the biopsy-confirmed check, and send the PASSION request now since it needs approval. Because the diagnosis mix differs by skin type in all of these, compare within condition.

All facts were checked on 2026-11-12 unless marked as from memory. The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-yIBc9C/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-fitzpatrick17k
graders.evidence:
Four public datasets meet your bar, each with a different weakness, and none gives you large, clinician-verified type VI numbers. I checked the counts below against the papers and repos today, except where marked.

| Dataset | Size and type | Skin tone label | Diagnosis label | V/VI representation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fitzpatrick17k** | 16,577 clinical photos from two online atlases | Fitzpatrick I–VI per image, assigned by non-expert annotators from the photo | 114 conditions, taken from atlas captions (noisy) | 1,533 type V and 635 type VI, about 13% |
| **DDI** (Stanford) | 656 clinical images | Fitzpatrick per image, released in three groups (I–II, III–IV, V–VI) | Pathologically confirmed | 207 V–VI images (159 benign, 48 malignant) |
| **PASSION** | 4,901 clinical images, 1,653 patients, sub-Saharan Africa, mostly paediatric | Fitzpatrick; cohort is IV–VI only | Eczema, fungal infections, scabies, impetigo | Essentially the whole dataset; I could not confirm per-type counts |
| **SCIN** (Google) | 10,000+ images, 5,033 crowdsourced US cases | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and layperson-estimated Monk | Weighted dermatologist differential over 419 conditions, on 2,835 cases | Self-reported: 9.8% V, 6.6% VI, but only 2,500 cases self-reported |

- **Fitzpatrick17k**: This is the largest dark-skin pool with broad disease coverage. A cleaned version, Fitzpatrick17k-C, keeps 11,394 images after removing duplicates and bad labels.
- **DDI**: It has the best label quality and was built for exactly this audit. It is small, though, so per-disease comparisons are underpowered, and one study noted it has no basal cell carcinoma in V–VI.
- **PASSION**: With no light-skin images, you would have to pair it with another dataset for the comparison, which confounds skin tone with site, camera and disease mix. The licence is CC BY-NC 4.0.
- **SCIN**: It is the only one with both scales. The dark-skin share depends heavily on which label you use: dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick gives only 5.3% V and 0.6% VI, and Monk 7–10 is under 2% by US labellers.

**DermaCon-IN** is a borderline fifth: 5,450 clinical images from about 3,000 patients in South India, with expert-assigned Fitzpatrick and Monk labels and 245 diagnoses. It skews to types IV and V, and I could not confirm how many type VI images it has. It is on Harvard Dataverse under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

These carry skin tone labels but fail your representation requirement:

- **MRA-MIDAS**: About 83% of its 796 patients are types I–II, and one preprint found zero V–VI cancers.
- **MILK10k**: It uses its own 0–5 tone scale, and only six cases carry the darkest label.
- **ISIC archive**: One group filtering by Fitzpatrick found 10 type V images and one type VI.
- **PAD-UFES-20**: From memory, not checked today, it has Fitzpatrick metadata but almost no V–VI.

For the audit itself, I would use DDI as the primary test set, since tone and diagnosis are both trustworthy. Fitzpatrick17k (cleaned) and SCIN then add breadth across non-cancer conditions, with results reported separately per dataset rather than pooled.

Sources:
- [Fitzpatrick17k paper (arXiv 2104.09957)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2104.09957)
- [CleanPatrick / Fitzpatrick17k-C (arXiv 2505.11034)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.11034)
- [Pipsqueak paper, with Fitzpatrick17k per-type counts and ISIC filtering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1877750326000761)
- [DDI paper (Science Advances)](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147)
- [PASSION paper (arXiv 2411.04584)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04584)
- [PASSION project repo](https://github.com/Digital-Dermatology/PASSION_project)
- [SCIN paper (arXiv 2402.18545)](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18545)
- [SCIN repo](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- [DermaCon-IN paper (arXiv 2506.06099)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099)
- [MIDAS paper (NEJM AI)](https://ai.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/AIdbp2400732)
- [MILK10k paper (JID)](https://www.jidonline.org/article/S0022-202X(25)02270-5/fulltext?rss=yes)
- [Colorimeter-supervised skin tone audit (arXiv 2602.10265)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10265v1)
- [Global Atlas of Digital Dermatology (arXiv 2601.00840)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.00840)

graders.name: 01-recall-fitzpatrick17k
graders.evidence:
Five public datasets fit your requirements, and none is clean on every axis, so a credible audit usually combines two or three. The counts below come from my recall of the papers plus a quick web check of summaries, not from downloading the data, so confirm them against the metadata files.

## Datasets that fit

| Dataset | Size | Skin tone label | Diagnosis label | Darker-skin (V–VI) representation | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fitzpatrick17k** | 16,577 clinical photos, 114 conditions | Fitzpatrick I–VI per image, by non-dermatologist annotators | Taken from the atlas sites, not biopsy-confirmed | About 1,530 type V and 635 type VI (13%) | GitHub; images scraped from two online atlases, non-commercial |
| **DDI (Diverse Dermatology Images)** | 656 clinical photos, 570 patients | Fitzpatrick per patient, only as groups I–II / III–IV / V–VI | Biopsy-proven, 78 diseases plus benign/malignant | 207 images in V–VI, balanced by design against 208 in I–II and 241 in III–IV | Stanford AIMI, research use agreement |
| **SCIN** | 10,000+ photos from 5,000+ US contributors | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick, and layperson-estimated Monk | Dermatologist differential diagnoses with confidence weights, no biopsy | Roughly 8.5% type V and 5.7% type VI per a secondary source; very few at Monk 8–10 | GitHub / Google Cloud bucket, open licence |
| **PASSION** | 4,901 phone photos, 1,653 patients, sub-Saharan Africa | Fitzpatrick per patient, IV–VI only | Common paediatric conditions (eczema, fungal, scabies, impetigo), dermatologist-checked | Essentially the whole dataset is dark skin | passionderm.github.io, own licence |
| **DermaCon-IN** | 5,450 clinical photos, about 3,000 patients, South India | Fitzpatrick and Monk per image, rated on unaffected skin | 245 dermatologist-assigned diagnoses in a hierarchy | Types IV and V dominate; type VI is thin | See the paper (NeurIPS 2025); I did not confirm the download location |

## What each is good for

- **DDI** is the cleanest test set: biopsy-proven and balanced, built for exactly this audit. It is small, and the grouped labels mean you cannot separate V from VI.
- **Fitzpatrick17k** gives the largest V–VI count across the most conditions. It has documented near-duplicates and label errors, so use the cleaned **Fitzpatrick17k-C** splits.
- **SCIN** is the only one with both scales, and it reflects consumer-style photos of mostly common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Its diagnoses are weighted differentials, so you need to decide how to score a "correct" answer.
- **PASSION** has no light-skin group, so it only works as the dark-skin arm of a comparison. Any gap against another dataset then mixes skin tone with site, camera and age (it is paediatric).
- **DermaCon-IN** fills the IV–V range well with dermatologist-rated tone on both scales, but adds little for type VI.

## Datasets that have the label but fail on representation

- **MIDAS** (Stanford, biopsy-proven, paired dermoscopy and clinical): Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only about 17% of patients are type III or above.
- **PAD-UFES-20** (Brazil, smartphone photos): Fitzpatrick is in the metadata for part of the set, with very few V–VI.
- **MILK10k** (ISIC, 5,240 lesions with clinical and dermoscopic pairs): it has its own six-level skin tone scale, deliberately not Fitzpatrick, and is mostly mid-range.
- **HAM10000, BCN20000, Derm7pt and most of the ISIC archive**: no skin tone label at all.

Dermoscopy is the weak spot: I know of no public dermoscopy set with substantial V–VI numbers, so in practice your audit will rest on clinical photos.

Sources:
- [SCIN GitHub repo](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- [SCIN paper (arXiv 2402.18545)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18545)
- [Secondary source for SCIN Fitzpatrick breakdown (arXiv 2510.00055)](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00055v2)
- [PASSION paper (arXiv 2411.04584)](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.04584v1)
- [DermaCon-IN paper (arXiv 2506.06099)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099)
- [MIDAS paper (NEJM AI)](https://ai.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/AIdbp2400732)

cases.name: ho-h-ecg-rhythm-labels
cases.promptMarkdown: I'm starting a project on automatically detecting atrial fibrillation and conduction problems (bundle branch blocks, AV block) from standard 10-second, 12-lead resting ECGs. I need at least a few thousand recordings that come with diagnostic labels, preferably assigned or confirmed by cardiologists. Our lab has no data use agreements or ethics approval set up yet, so it has to be something I can download this week without applying or getting credentialed. What are my best options?

graders.name: 01-recall-ptbxl
graders.evidence:
You can start today: four large, openly downloadable sets meet all your must-haves, and PTB-XL is the best first download. Access and licence were checked on 12 November 2026 against each host's own record; anything I'm relying on from memory is marked.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** standard 12-lead resting ECG, about 10 seconds.
- **R2 (must):** diagnostic labels for AF, bundle branch blocks and AV block.
- **R3 (must):** at least a few thousand recordings.
- **R4 (must):** direct download, with no application, credentialing, ethics approval or signed agreement.
- **R5 (nice):** labels assigned or confirmed by cardiologists.
- **R6 (nice):** licence allows research use and publication. I assumed academic use and adult patients.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PTB-XL | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 21,799 ECGs / 18,869 patients | Strong | today |
| 2 | Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo ("A large scale 12-lead ECG database for arrhythmia study") | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 45,152 patients | Strong | today |
| 3 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 collection | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | about 88,000 ECGs (from memory), 13.6 GB | Strong | today |
| 4 | CODE-15% | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 345,779 ECGs / 233,770 patients | Strong | today |
| 5 | SPH (Shandong Provincial Hospital) | Direct download, from memory; figshare blocked the check | CC BY 4.0 | 25,770 ECGs / 24,666 patients | Strong, access unconfirmed | DOI today, access from memory |
| 6 | CODE-test | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 827 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | today |
| 7 | Conduction-abnormality test set (Mendeley Data) | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 828 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | today |
| 8 | MIMIC-IV-ECG | Direct download, no account | ODbL 1.0 | about 800,000 ECGs / 160,000 patients | Partial (machine labels) | today |

## Details

**1. PTB-XL** — https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** 10-second clinical 12-lead ECGs, "annotated by up to two cardiologists", with recommended train/test folds.
- **Your classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, 800 first-degree AV block, 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, and 1,100 incomplete RBBB. Second- and third-degree AV block have only about a dozen each.
- **Limits:** not every record was human-validated (filter on `validated_by_human`), and it is a single German source from 1989–1996.
- **Papers:** the data descriptor (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6) and a benchmark with baselines (https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989).

**2. Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo** — https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/
- **Contents:** 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz from two Chinese hospitals; 10-second length is from memory.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician settling disagreements. These are physicians, not stated to be cardiologists.
- **Note:** it supersedes the 2019 figshare release of 10,646 patients, which is a subset.

**3. Challenge 2021 collection** — https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** one download pooling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes.
- **Why use it:** it is the easiest route to multi-site training, and the Georgia (US) set exists only here.
- **Limits:** it contains #1 and #2, so never treat those as independent test data. Label quality varies by source, and some parts are longer than 10 seconds.
- **Paper:** a meta-analysis of the 2020 edition (https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. CODE-15%** — https://zenodo.org/records/4916206
- **Contents:** Brazilian telehealth ECGs with six binary labels; the page confirms an AF column, and RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block are from memory.
- **Labels (from memory):** derived from the cardiologist report combined with automated analysis, with manual review of disagreements.
- **Limits:** traces are 7–10 seconds at 400 Hz, zero-padded to 4,096 samples. There is no higher-degree AV block label.
- **Paper:** https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4.

**5. SPH** — https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802
- **Contents:** records of 10–60 seconds at 500 Hz, labelled with AHA/ACC/HRS standard statements.
- **Check first:** open the page in a browser to confirm it downloads freely, and read the descriptor for who assigned the labels.

**6. CODE-test** — https://zenodo.org/records/3765780
- **Labels:** the cleanest on the list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", with a third senior specialist as tiebreak.
- **Use:** a test set. It comes from the same network as CODE-15%, so it is not fully external for models trained on that.

**7. Conduction test set** — https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists … annotated by consensus".
- **Limits:** I did not read the exact class list, and it mixes in some Holter-derived traces.

**8. MIMIC-IV-ECG** — https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/
- **Contents:** 10-second 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz, 97 GB; the page says "the project access has been changed to open".
- **Limits:** the open labels are the ECG machine's automated statements. The cardiologist reports and the ICD label extension need credentialed access.
- **Use:** pretraining, not ground truth. ODbL means any derived database must carry the same licence.

## Known, not confirmed
- **ZZU critical-value ECG dataset** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31229326.v3): 20,126 records from 9,785 patients, 7–198 seconds, 15 critical arrhythmia types "labeled and verified by professional physicians". The DOI is registered with CC BY 4.0, but figshare blocked the page. It might add high-degree AV block cases, so check the class list.
- **CPSC2018 standalone:** the registry record I found returned a 404, and I did not verify the official challenge site. The data is inside #3 anyway.

## Not recommended, and why
- **KURIAS-ECG:** needs a signed agreement, and the page says the authors "have asked for downloads to be disabled until further notice".
- **MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD and Harvard-Emory ECG Database:** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files."
- **Full CODE cohort (2.3 M ECGs):** by application to the authors (from memory).
- **EchoNext:** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease.
- **PTB Diagnostic, MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, MIT-BIH AF, Challenge 2017, INCART:** open, but too small or not 10-second resting 12-lead recordings.
- **ZZU pediatric ECG database:** children aged 0–14.
- **Hugging Face copies of these sets:** third-party mirrors, one of which states licence terms that do not match the source. Use the official hosts.

## What I could not find
- No open set has enough second- or third-degree AV block for a dedicated classifier. Pooling #1, #2 and #5 is the best you can do without an application.
- No open North American set has cardiologist-confirmed labels.
- Dataset-specific paper lookups for CODE-15%, Chapman and SPH returned nothing useful, so those entries have fewer usage references.

## Next step
Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today, train on one and test on the other, and use CODE-test as a cardiologist-consensus check. Add CODE-15% when you need scale. Open data may still need an exemption determination from your institution, so ask early.

The interactive page with per-requirement evidence is at `/private/tmp/e-uHEHsn/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **CPSC 2018 original site:** it returned a server error today. The data (6,877 records, from memory) is inside the Challenge 2021 collection.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg-ext-icd-labels/):** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files".

- **[CODE full dataset](https://doi.org/10.17044/scilifelab.15169716.v1):** individual request, then a data user agreement.

- **Hugging Face and Zenodo re-uploads:** third-party copies; use the official sources.

- An open dataset with many cardiologist-confirmed second- or third-degree AV block cases. Open data mainly supports first-degree AV block.
- A large open US or European set with uniformly cardiologist-confirmed labels beyond PTB-XL.

Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today (under 9 GB together) and train on those. Hold out SPH and CODE-test as external test sets, and add Georgia from the Challenge 2021 collection for a US population. Even for open de-identified data, ask your institution early whether it needs an exempt determination before you publish.

It might add high-grade AV block cases. The DOI is registered, but figshare refused automated reading, so check the class list in a browser.
- **CPSC 2018 original site:** it returned a server error today. The data (6,877 records, from memory) is inside the Challenge 2021 collection.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg-ext-icd-labels/):** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files".
- **[Harvard-Emory ECG Database](https://bdsp.io/content/heedb/):** credentialed access plus a data use agreement.
- **[CODE full dataset](https://doi.org/10.17044/scilifelab.15169716.v1):** individual request, then a data user agreement.
- **[KURIAS-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/kurias-ecg/1.0/):** "Only registered users who sign the specified data use agreement can access the files". This is a click-through with no reviewer, so it becomes usable if you relax R5.
- **[EchoNext](https://physionet.org/content/echonext/1.1.1/):** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease, not rhythm or conduction.
- **[Challenge 2020](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2020/1.0.2/) and the [Chapman figshare release](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4560497):** open, but contained in datasets 3 and 2.
- **[Sami-Trop](https://zenodo.org/records/4905618):** open, but annotated with age and mortality only.
- **MIT-BIH, INCART, Challenge 2017, LUDB:** ambulatory, single-lead, or too small.
- **Hugging Face and Zenodo re-uploads:** third-party copies; use the official sources.

## What I could not find
- An open dataset with many cardiologist-confirmed second- or third-degree AV block cases. Open data mainly supports first-degree AV block.
- A large open US or European set with uniformly cardiologist-confirmed labels beyond PTB-XL.

## Next step
Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today (under 9 GB together) and train on those. Hold out SPH and CODE-test as external test sets, and add Georgia from the Challenge 2021 collection for a US population. Even for open de-identified data, ask your institution early whether it needs an exempt determination before you publish.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-GYPTSy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **R1 (must):** 12-lead resting ECG waveforms of about 10 seconds.
- **R2 (must):** diagnostic labels covering AF, bundle branch blocks and AV block.
- **R3 (nice):** labels assigned or confirmed by cardiologists.
- **R4 (must):** at least a few thousand recordings.
- **R5 (must):** downloadable now, with no application, credentialing, data use agreement or ethics approval. I treated a click-through agreement as failing this.
- **R6 (assumed):** licence allows research use and publication.

## Shortlist
Access and licence were checked today (12 Nov 2026) for every row; "from memory" marks label or count details I did not re-read.

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PTB-XL | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 21,799 ECGs, 3.2 GB | Strong | today; class counts from memory |
| 2 | Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 45,152 ECGs, 5.5 GB | Strong | today; AF and AV-block labels from memory |
| 3 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | about 88,000 ECGs, 13.6 GB | Strong | today; composition from memory |
| 4 | SPH (Shandong Provincial Hospital) | Direct download from figshare | CC BY 4.0 | 25,770 ECGs | Strong | registry record today; page not readable by script |
| 5 | CODE-15% | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 345,779 exams, 46 GB | Partial | today; label provenance from memory |
| 6 | CODE-test | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 827 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | today |
| 7 | Mendeley conduction test set | Direct download (not tested) | CC BY 4.0 | 828 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | registry record today |
| 8 | MIMIC-IV-ECG | Direct download, no account | ODbL 1.0 | about 800,000 ECGs, 97 GB | Partial (no expert labels) | today |

## Details

**1. [PTB-XL](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** "21799 clinical 12-lead ECGs from 18869 patients of 10 second length", from one German site.
- **Labels:** "annotated by up to two cardiologists", but some reports are "automatic interpretation by ECG-device". Filter on the `validated_by_human` column.
- **Classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, about 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, about 800 first-degree AV block, and under 20 each of second- and third-degree.
- **Splits:** use the provided `strat_fold` column, which keeps each patient in one fold.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6), [benchmarks](https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989), [AF detection](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijcard.2020.11.053).

**2. [Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo](https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/)**
- **Contents:** "12-lead ECGs of 45,152 patients with a 500 Hz sampling rate", 10-second readings, from two Chinese hospitals.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician resolving disagreements. The page says physicians, not cardiologists.
- **Classes:** RBBB and LBBB are named on the page; AF and AV-block labels are from memory.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor of the first part](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0386-x), [rhythm classification](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-59821-7).

**3. [PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** one collection bundling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC 2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes (composition from memory).
- **Why use it:** it is the only route I know to Georgia (about 10,000 US ECGs) and CPSC 2018, and it makes cross-site testing easy.
- **Caveats:** it contains datasets 1 and 2, so de-duplicate before combining. Some sources are not 10 seconds, and label quality varies by source.
- **Papers:** [organisers on label heterogeneity](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6579/ac79fd), [meta-analysis of the 2020 methods](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. [SPH](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802.v1)**
- **Contents:** "25770 12-lead clinical ECG records from 24666 patients", 500 Hz, "length of records ranges from 10 to 60 seconds", so crop to 10 seconds.
- **Labels:** 44 primary statements in the AHA/ACC/HRS standard. Cardiologist labelling is from memory; I did not check per-class counts.
- **Why use it:** it is independent of the Challenge collection, so it works as an external test set.
- **Access:** open the link in a browser; figshare blocks scripts.
- **Paper:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01403-5).

**5. [CODE-15%](https://zenodo.org/records/4916206)**
- **Contents:** "345 779 exams from 233 770 patients" from Brazilian primary care, at 400 Hz; traces are 7 or 10 seconds, zero-padded.
- **Labels:** columns for AF, RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block only.
- **Label provenance (from memory):** derived from the reporting cardiologist's text combined with automated analysis, with manual review only on disagreement.
- **Paper:** [the CODE model and labelling](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4).

**6. [CODE-test](https://zenodo.org/records/3765780)**
- **Contents:** 827 tracings with the same six classes as CODE-15%.
- **Labels:** the cleanest on this list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", otherwise a third senior specialist decided.
- **Use:** evaluation only.

**7. [Mendeley conduction test set](https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1)**
- **Contents:** 828 "standard 10-second, 12-lead ECGs" at 500 Hz.
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists ... annotated by consensus". I did not read the class list, so check it before relying on it.

**8. [MIMIC-IV-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/)**
- **Contents:** about 800,000 ECGs: "12 leads and are 10 seconds in length", 500 Hz.
- **Access:** "the project access has been changed to open instead of requiring credentialling".
- **Labels:** machine statements only in the open release. The cardiologist reports are consortium-only, and the ICD label set needs credentialing.
- **Use:** pretraining now; labelled work later if you get credentialed. ODbL is share-alike for derived datasets.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[ZZU critical-value ECG dataset](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31229326.v3):** 20,126 records, 7–198 seconds, 15 critical arrhythmias, "labeled and verified by professional physicians", CC BY 4.0. It might add high-grade AV block cases. The DOI is registered, but figshare refused automated reading, so check the class list in a browser.
- **CPSC 2018 original site:** it returned a server error today. The data (6,877 records, from memory) is inside the Challenge 2021 collection.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg-ext-icd-labels/):** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files".
- **[Harvard-Emory ECG Database](https://bdsp.io/content/heedb/):** credentialed access plus a data use agreement.
- **[CODE full dataset](https://doi.org/10.17044/scilifelab.15169716.v1):** individual request, then a data user agreement.
- **[KURIAS-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/kurias-ecg/1.0/):** "Only registered users who sign the specified data use agreement can access the files". This is a click-through with no reviewer, so it becomes usable if you relax R5.
- **[EchoNext](https://physionet.org/content/echonext/1.1.1/):** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease, not rhythm or conduction.
- **[Challenge 2020](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2020/1.0.2/) and the [Chapman figshare release](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4560497):** open, but contained in datasets 3 and 2.
- **[Sami-Trop](https://zenodo.org/records/4905618):** open, but annotated with age and mortality only.
- **MIT-BIH, INCART, Challenge 2017, LUDB:** ambulatory, single-lead, or too small.
- **Hugging Face and Zenodo re-uploads:** third-party copies; use the official sources.

## What I could not find
- An open dataset with many cardiologist-confirmed second- or third-degree AV block cases. Open data mainly supports first-degree AV block.
- A large open US or European set with uniformly cardiologist-confirmed labels beyond PTB-XL.

## Next step
Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today (under 9 GB together) and train on those. Hold out SPH and CODE-test as external test sets, and add Georgia from the Challenge 2021 collection for a US population. Even for open de-identified data, ask your institution early whether it needs an exempt determination before you publish.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-GYPTSy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 09-long-tail
graders.evidence:
You can do this with fully open data: several large 12-lead sets are downloadable today with no application or credentialing, all under CC BY 4.0 as far as I recall. This is from memory, not re-checked against the live pages today, so treat the counts as approximate and confirm the licence on each landing page.

| Dataset | Where | Size | Labels | Fit for your targets |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Dataset | Size | Format | Labels | Fit for AF / BBB / AV block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[PTB-XL](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/)** v1.0.3 | 21,799 records, 18,869 patients | 10 s, 500 Hz (and 100 Hz) | Annotated by up to two cardiologists | Best label quality. From memory: about 1,500 AF, 500 each complete LBBB and RBBB, 800 first-degree AV block, only a few dozen second- and third-degree. |
| **[Chapman-Shaoxing + Ningbo](https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/)** v1.0.0 | 45,152 patient ECGs | 10 s, 500 Hz | Physician-labelled, second physician validated, senior physician resolved disagreements | Strong for AF and other rhythms; includes LBBB and RBBB. I did not confirm the AV block labels. |
| **[PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/)** v1.0.3 | 88,253 public training records | Mostly 10 s, 500 Hz | Varies by source; some are machine labels overread by humans | Largest pool, with all labels mapped to SNOMED-CT codes. |
| **[CODE-15%](https://zenodo.org/records/4916206)** | 345,779 exams, 233,770 patients | 7–10 s, 400 Hz, zero-padded | Semi-automatic (from memory: cardiologist report text combined with automatic analysis) | Label set is almost exactly your targets: AF, RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block, plus sinus bradycardia and tachycardia. |

- **Start with PTB-XL.** It has the cleanest cardiologist labels and ships recommended patient-level folds (`strat_fold`), so you can have a baseline quickly.
- **Add Chapman-Shaoxing-Ningbo for volume.** It gives you more AF and bundle branch block cases from a different population and device, which also makes it useful as an external test set.
- **Use Challenge 2021 only if you want one harmonised download.** It already contains PTB-XL and Chapman-Ningbo, so don't count those twice. What it adds is CPSC 2018 (10,330 training records including CPSC-Extra) and Georgia (10,344). The organisers warn that some labels are wrong.
- **Use CODE-15% for scale or pretraining.** Its labels are noisier, so treat it as training data rather than a benchmark. From memory, the companion CODE test set on Zenodo (827 ECGs with cardiologist-consensus labels on the same six classes) is a good held-out benchmark.

Two limits apply whichever you choose:

- **High-grade AV block is rare everywhere.** First-degree is well covered, but second- and third-degree cases number in the tens per dataset. If you need them, plan to pool sources or scope the task to first-degree block.
- **Open access does not settle your own ethics position.** These are de-identified public datasets, which many institutions treat as exempt, but your institution may still want a formal determination before you publish.

I left out MIMIC-IV-ECG: its labels are machine-generated statements, and linking it to clinical data requires credentialing.

cases.name: ho-h-measured-bp-surveys
cases.promptMarkdown: I'm writing an epidemiology thesis chapter on hypertension awareness, i.e. what share of adults with high blood pressure don't know they have it. For that I need nationally representative survey data where blood pressure was actually measured by a nurse or examiner, alongside a question on whether a doctor ever told them they have high blood pressure. Self-reported hypertension on its own is useless to me. US data would be ideal, but I'd also like one or two comparable national surveys from other countries (samples of middle-aged and older adults are fine). Which surveys should I use, and what do I have to do to get each one?

graders.name: 01-recall-nhanes
graders.evidence:
Use NHANES for the US, and ELSA (England, ages 50+) and CHARLS (China, ages 45+) as the comparison surveys. All three have measured blood pressure and a "doctor ever told you" question, and a 2026 paper already runs the hypertension cascade across exactly these three. I checked what I could on 12 November 2026; the HRS and CHARLS sites would not open from here, so their terms rest on search snippets and memory.

## What I assumed you need
- **Must have:** blood pressure measured by a nurse or examiner.
- **Must have:** a question on ever being told by a doctor that you have high blood pressure.
- **Must have:** a nationally representative sample with weights.
- **Nice to have:** all adults (you said middle-aged and older is acceptable).
- **Nice to have (my assumption):** obtainable by a thesis student without an institutional contract.

## Shortlist
| # | Survey | Access | Licence | Sample | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES (US) | Direct download, minutes | NCHS Data User Agreement | All ages, 2-year cycles 1999–2023 | Strong | Today |
| 2 | ELSA (England) | Free UK Data Service account, days | End User Licence | Ages 50+ | Strong | Today; diagnosis item from memory |
| 3 | HRS (US) | Free account, days | HRS Conditions of Use | Ages 51+ | Strong, but interviewer-measured | Search snippets and memory |
| 4 | Health Survey for England | Free UK Data Service account, days | End User Licence | Ages 16+, annual | Strong | Record exists today; contents from memory |
| 5 | KNHANES (Korea) | Free registration, days | KDCA terms, no redistribution | All ages, annual | Strong | Search snippets |
| 6 | CHARLS (China) | Registration plus application, days | CHARLS data use agreement | Ages 45+ | Strong, 2011–2015 only | Partly today, rest from memory |
| 7 | LASI Wave 1 (India) | Request form to IIPS, weeks (my estimate) | IIPS release terms | 72,250 aged 45+ and spouses | Strong | Search snippets of the IIPS form |
| 8 | DHS (selected countries) | Project request, 24–48 h | DHS conditions of use | Varies by country | Partial | Today |

## Details

**1. NHANES** — https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/
- **Blood pressure:** the August 2021–August 2023 file (BPXO_L) has "three consecutive blood pressure (BP) and pulse measurements using an oscillometric device", taken by certified examiners.
- **Awareness question:** BPQ020, "ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that you had hypertension, also called high blood pressure?"
- **Access:** download the DEMO, BPQ and BPX/BPXO files per cycle, no login. Using the files means you accept the NCHS Data User Agreement (statistical use only, no re-identification).
- **Watch for:** older cycles used physician auscultatory readings and recent ones use oscillometric devices. Check the cut-over before building a trend; I recall it but did not confirm it.
- **Used in:** [Hypertension, Diabetes, and High Cholesterol Awareness Among US Adults (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamacardio.2025.1536).

**2. ELSA** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-5050-37
- **Blood pressure:** nurse visit files at waves 2, 4, 6 and 8/9, plus a wave 11 nurse file, with three readings each.
- **Awareness question:** doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure in the main interview (from memory; check the wave questionnaire).
- **Access:** register with the UK Data Service, accept the End User Licence and download study 5050. Outside the UK you "apply for a username and then register"; no turnaround time is stated.
- **Watch for:** UKDS says some collections are closed to non-UK users, so check the Access tab of the record. The wave 8 nurse visit covered only part of the sample.
- **Used in:** [the China/US/UK care cascade comparison (2026)](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14040501).

**3. HRS** — https://hrsdata.isr.umich.edu/
- **Blood pressure:** Section I of the public core file. From memory, it is taken by trained interviewers, not nurses, on alternating half-samples since 2006; decide whether that meets your criterion.
- **Awareness question:** "Has a doctor ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?" (from memory).
- **Access:** free registration, which counts as accepting the Conditions of Use (no re-identification, no redistribution).
- **Used in:** [a four-country hypertension analysis with ELSA, CHARLS and LASI (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1161/jaha.123.030765).

**4. Health Survey for England** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-9469-1 (2022)
- **Why:** the all-adult English counterpart to NHANES, with one study per year.
- **Access:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Watch for:** the nurse-visit BP and diagnosis question are from memory, as is the gap in 2020. Check each year's documentation.

**5. KNHANES** — https://knhanes.kdca.go.kr/knhanes/eng/main.do
- **Why:** measured BP and a physician-diagnosis item; this is the source of Korea's official awareness rates.
- **Access:** register on the KDCA site and download yearly files. I could not read the registration page, so the exact steps are unconfirmed.
- **Used in:** [a 2022–2024 care cascade paper](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14193198).

**6. CHARLS** — https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/ (did not answer today)
- **Blood pressure:** measured "at Waves 1 through 3" (2011, 2013, 2015) only, by trained interviewers.
- **Access:** register, submit an application with your research purpose and accept the agreement. Approval takes a few days, from memory. Derived files may not be redistributed.
- **Help:** the [Gateway to Global Aging page](https://g2aging.org/additional-resources/gateway-blog/05a8df66-b9ab-47de-879e-b0bde672798d) links step-by-step instructions.

**7. LASI Wave 1** — https://iipsindia.ac.in/content/lasi-wave-i
- **Contents:** three Omron readings, and item HT002 on ever being told of hypertension.
- **Access:** send IIPS the [data request form](https://iipsindia.ac.in/sites/default/files/LASI_DataRequestForm_0.pdf) with a research description of up to 500 words, a study proposal and identity proof.

**8. DHS** — https://dhsprogram.com/data/
- **Why:** an option for a low- or middle-income comparison; only some rounds carry a BP module (Bangladesh 2017–18 and 2022 do).
- **Access:** register, submit a project title and description, and wait for review "within 24 – 48 hours".
- **Used in:** [a Bangladesh hypertension control paper (2026)](https://doi.org/10.5334/gh.1575).

## Known, not confirmed
These fit as far as I recall, but I did not check their contents today:
- **Indonesia Family Life Survey:** the RAND site blocked the tool.
- **WHO SAGE and WHO STEPS surveys:** the pages exist, and STEPS is used for awareness in recent papers.
- **TILDA (Ireland):** the site did not respond.
- **Understanding Society nurse assessment (UK, 2010–2012) and the Scottish Health Survey:** the UK Data Service records exist.

## Not recommended, and why
- **BRFSS and NHIS:** self-report only (from memory).
- **SHARE:** no routine measured BP (from memory).
- **UK Biobank:** a volunteer cohort, not representative.
- **Canadian Health Measures Survey:** I recall the microdata sit in Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, which is slow from outside Canada.
- **Mexican Health and Aging Study:** BP only in subsamples (from memory). Its terms also forbid using LLM or AI tools on the microdata.

## What I could not find
- The registry search returned mostly noise for this topic; the list comes from known surveys, the literature and web search.
- I did not find a harmonised cross-country file that includes measured BP ready-made; the Gateway to Global Aging may have one, but I did not check.

## Next step
Download NHANES today and register with the UK Data Service and CHARLS in parallel, since those two involve waiting. The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-FtUsPb/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.
