graders.name: 01-recall-nhanes
graders.evidence:
Use **NHANES** as your US core, **HRS** if you want a US 50+ estimate, and **ELSA** (England 50+) plus either **Health Survey for England** or **KNHANES** as the international comparators. All of these are free and need at most an online registration. Checked on 12 November 2026.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** blood pressure measured by a nurse or trained examiner.
- **R2 (must):** a question on ever being told by a doctor that they have high blood pressure.
- **R3 (must):** a nationally representative adult sample; 45+/50+ is acceptable outside the US.
- **R4 (nice to have):** obtainable by a thesis student without an institutional contract. This is my assumption.

## Shortlist
| # | Survey | Country, ages | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES | US, all adults | Direct download, no account | NCHS data user agreement (statistical use only, no re-identification) | Strong | Today |
| 2 | HRS | US, 51+ | Free registration, minutes to a day | HRS conditions of use | Strong | Access from search results; the HRS site blocks automated readers |
| 3 | ELSA | England, 50+ | UK Data Service registration, minutes to days | End User Licence, non-commercial | Strong | Access today; nurse-wave detail from memory |
| 4 | Health Survey for England 2019 | England, 16+ | UK Data Service registration, minutes to days | End User Licence, non-commercial | Strong | Mostly today |
| 5 | CHARLS | China, 45+ | Free registration with approval, days | CHARLS data use agreement | Strong | Via Gateway to Global Aging; the CHARLS site was down |
| 6 | LASI Wave 1 | India, 45+ | Request form plus photo ID, 24–48 h review | Academic research only | Strong | Today |
| 7 | KNHANES | South Korea, all ages | Free download after accepting terms | KDCA terms | Strong | Access from memory |
| 8 | CHMS | Canada, 6–79 | Secure Research Data Centre only, months | Statistics Canada research agreement | Partial | Today |

## Details

**1. NHANES** — https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/
- **Blood pressure:** certified examiners take three readings 60 seconds apart with an Omron HEM-907XL in the mobile examination centre (August 2021–August 2023 cycle).
- **Awareness item:** BPQ020, "ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that you had hypertension, also called high blood pressure?", asked of ages 16+.
- **Steps:** download the DEMO, BPXO and BPQ files for each cycle, merge on SEQN, and use the examination weights. There is no account or fee.
- **Caveats:** auscultatory (mercury) readings stopped after 2017–2018 and later cycles are oscillometric, which matters for trends. From memory, a combined 2017–March 2020 pre-pandemic file also exists.
- **Used in:** [care-cascade comparison of China, the US and the UK](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14040501) (NHANES, CHARLS, ELSA).

**2. HRS** — https://hrs.isr.umich.edu/data-products
- **Blood pressure:** measured in the home by trained interviewers, not nurses, since 2006. It sits in section I of the public core files, not in the sensitive-health tier.
- **Awareness item:** from memory, "Has a doctor ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"; check section C of the questionnaire.
- **Steps:** register at hrsdata.isr.umich.edu, accept the conditions of use, and download the core files plus the Tracker file for the physical-measures weights.
- **Caveats:** a random half of the sample gets the in-person visit each wave, so pool adjacent waves. The conditions of use reportedly now include a policy on AI and language-model tools; read it before using hosted tools on the data.
- **Used in:** [HRS blood pressure control study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8824637/); [five-cohort hypertension care cascade in adults 50+](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-26341-4).

**3. ELSA** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-5050-37 (UK Data Service SN 5050)
- **Why:** it is the sister study of HRS, so it gives the cleanest comparison with a US 50+ estimate.
- **Blood pressure:** from memory, nurse visits with blood pressure are in waves 2, 4, 6 and 8/9 and are in the standard files. I could not confirm this today because the UK Data Service catalogue is not machine-readable.
- **Steps:** register with the UK Data Service (request a username if your university is not in the UK login federation), accept the End User Licence, add SN 5050 to a project with a short statement of intended use, and download.
- **Caveats:** England only; non-commercial use; no onward sharing.

**4. Health Survey for England 2019** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-8860-1 (SN 8860)
- **Why:** an all-adult annual cross-section with a nurse visit, the closest non-US analogue to NHANES.
- **Blood pressure:** the catalogue records list it among the nurse-collected measurements.
- **Awareness item:** doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure questions are in the interview, from memory.
- **Steps:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Caveats:** since 2015 the standard release is the individual file only, and some variables moved to the Special Licence version (SN 8962). Check that the blood pressure variables you need are in SN 8860. The 2021 and 2022 surveys exist, but I did not confirm they had a full nurse visit.

**5. CHARLS** — https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/ (site unreachable today)
- **Blood pressure:** measured in waves 1–3 (2011, 2013, 2015).
- **Awareness item:** a doctor-diagnosed hypertension question, from memory.
- **Steps:** register on the CHARLS site with your institution and purpose, accept the agreement, wait for approval (a few days, from memory), then download. The [Gateway to Global Aging page](https://g2aging.org/additional-resources/gateway-blog/05a8df66-b9ab-47de-879e-b0bde672798d) links step-by-step instructions.

**6. LASI Wave 1** — https://www.iipsindia.ac.in/content/LASI-data
- **Blood pressure:** three readings in the biomarker module.
- **Awareness item:** "Has any health professional ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"
- **Steps:** follow the LASI Wave 1 Dataset link to the IIPS data portal, submit the request form with government-issued ID, and wait for review (24–48 working hours).
- **Caveat:** one wave only (2017–19, from memory).

**7. KNHANES** — https://knhanes.kdca.go.kr/knhanes/eng/main.do
- **Blood pressure:** three readings by a trained nurse.
- **Awareness item:** self-reported physician diagnosis.
- **Steps:** from memory, open the raw-data section, enter an email, accept the terms, and download the yearly SAS/SPSS files. The English page did not show these steps today, so confirm in a browser.
- **Used in:** [awareness trends in South Korea, 1998–2021](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-49055-8).

**8. CHMS** — https://crdcn.ca/data/canadian-health-measures-survey/
- **Blood pressure:** six oscillometric readings at a mobile centre.
- **Access:** microdata are analysed only inside Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, after a project proposal and security screening. In practice this needs a Canadian affiliation.
- **Alternative:** for a comparison figure, cite the published estimates in [Health Reports 2019](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/82-003-x/2019002/article/00002-eng.pdf).

## Known, not confirmed
- **NSHAP** (US, older adults; Round 4 2021–23 at https://doi.org/10.3886/icpsr39511.v1): the record exists. Measured blood pressure, a hypertension-diagnosis item and download with a free ICPSR account are all from memory.
- **DHS Program** (https://dhsprogram.com/data/): "Datasets are available for free after a simple registration process." Only some country surveys include measured blood pressure; papers found today used Bangladesh 2017–18 and 2022 and Tanzania 2022.
- **WHO STEPS surveys** (https://extranet.who.int/ncdsmicrodata/index.php/catalog): the catalogue exists and a Sri Lanka 2021 analysis turned up today. Per-country access terms were not checked.
- **TILDA** (Ireland, 50+): withdrawn from ICPSR at the producer's request. It is now available only through TILDA/ISSDA to non-commercial applicants, with an application form and fees listed. I did not confirm that blood pressure is in the public file.
- **Add Health, IFLS, MHAS:** all have measured blood pressure from memory; I checked neither access nor fit.

## Not recommended, and why
- **NHIS and BRFSS:** self-reported hypertension only, with no measured blood pressure (from memory).
- **SHARE:** no measured blood pressure in the main waves (from memory).

## What I could not find
- The HRS, UK Data Service and CHARLS pages could not be read by machine today, so open each in a browser to confirm the terms.
- The exact wording of the ever-told item is confirmed only for NHANES and LASI.
- The general data registries returned nothing useful, because these surveys are published on agency and archive sites.

## Next step
Download NHANES today and start the US analysis. In parallel, register with the UK Data Service and HRS; both are short forms. Before pooling cycles or countries, fix one definition of hypertension (threshold, and whether medication use counts), because the awareness denominator depends on it. Also ask your institution whether secondary analysis of these files needs an ethics exemption.

The interactive shortlist with filters and an exportable access plan is at `/private/tmp/e-pzWgGy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

**4. Health Survey for England 2019** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-8860-1 (SN 8860)
- **Why:** an all-adult annual cross-section with a nurse visit, the closest non-US analogue to NHANES.
- **Blood pressure:** the catalogue records list it among the nurse-collected measurements.
- **Awareness item:** doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure questions are in the interview, from memory.
- **Steps:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Caveats:** since 2015 the standard release is the individual file only, and some variables moved to the Special Licence version (SN 8962). Check that the blood pressure variables you need are in SN 8860. The 2021 and 2022 surveys exist, but I did not confirm they had a full nurse visit.

**5. CHARLS** — https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/ (site unreachable today)
- **Blood pressure:** measured in waves 1–3 (2011, 2013, 2015).
- **Awareness item:** a doctor-diagnosed hypertension question, from memory.
- **Steps:** register on the CHARLS site with your institution and purpose, accept the agreement, wait for approval (a few days, from memory), then download. The [Gateway to Global Aging page](https://g2aging.org/additional-resources/gateway-blog/05a8df66-b9ab-47de-879e-b0bde672798d) links step-by-step instructions.

**6. LASI Wave 1** — https://www.iipsindia.ac.in/content/LASI-data
- **Blood pressure:** three readings in the biomarker module.
- **Awareness item:** "Has any health professional ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"
- **Steps:** follow the LASI Wave 1 Dataset link to the IIPS data portal, submit the request form with government-issued ID, and wait for review (24–48 working hours).
- **Caveat:** one wave only (2017–19, from memory).

**7. KNHANES** — https://knhanes.kdca.go.kr/knhanes/eng/main.do
- **Blood pressure:** three readings by a trained nurse.
- **Awareness item:** self-reported physician diagnosis.
- **Steps:** from memory, open the raw-data section, enter an email, accept the terms, and download the yearly SAS/SPSS files. The English page did not show these steps today, so confirm in a browser.
- **Used in:** [awareness trends in South Korea, 1998–2021](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-49055-8).

**8. CHMS** — https://crdcn.ca/data/canadian-health-measures-survey/
- **Blood pressure:** six oscillometric readings at a mobile centre.
- **Access:** microdata are analysed only inside Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, after a project proposal and security screening. In practice this needs a Canadian affiliation.
- **Alternative:** for a comparison figure, cite the published estimates in [Health Reports 2019](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/82-003-x/2019002/article/00002-eng.pdf).

## Known, not confirmed
- **NSHAP** (US, older adults; Round 4 2021–23 at https://doi.org/10.3886/icpsr39511.v1): the record exists. Measured blood pressure, a hypertension-diagnosis item and download with a free ICPSR account are all from memory.
- **DHS Program** (https://dhsprogram.com/data/): "Datasets are available for free after a simple registration process." Only some country surveys include measured blood pressure; papers found today used Bangladesh 2017–18 and 2022 and Tanzania 2022.
- **WHO STEPS surveys** (https://extranet.who.int/ncdsmicrodata/index.php/catalog): the catalogue exists and a Sri Lanka 2021 analysis turned up today. Per-country access terms were not checked.
- **TILDA** (Ireland, 50+): withdrawn from ICPSR at the producer's request. It is now available only through TILDA/ISSDA to non-commercial applicants, with an application form and fees listed. I did not confirm that blood pressure is in the public file.
- **Add Health, IFLS, MHAS:** all have measured blood pressure from memory; I checked neither access nor fit.

## Not recommended, and why
- **NHIS and BRFSS:** self-reported hypertension only, with no measured blood pressure (from memory).
- **SHARE:** no measured blood pressure in the main waves (from memory).

## What I could not find
- The HRS, UK Data Service and CHARLS pages could not be read by machine today, so open each in a browser to confirm the terms.
- The exact wording of the ever-told item is confirmed only for NHANES and LASI.
- The general data registries returned nothing useful, because these surveys are published on agency and archive sites.

## Next step
Download NHANES today and start the US analysis. In parallel, register with the UK Data Service and HRS; both are short forms. Before pooling cycles or countries, fix one definition of hypertension (threshold, and whether medication use counts), because the awareness denominator depends on it. Also ask your institution whether secondary analysis of these files needs an ethics exemption.

The interactive shortlist with filters and an exportable access plan is at `/private/tmp/e-pzWgGy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-nhanes
graders.evidence:
**Use NHANES as your US source, and add KNHANES (South Korea) and the Health Survey for England as comparators.** All three measure blood pressure in a standardized exam and ask the "ever told by a doctor" question. This is from memory, not checked against the current sites, so confirm variable names and the latest release in each codebook.

| Survey | Population | BP measurement | Diagnosis question | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NHANES** (US, CDC/NCHS) | All ages, 2-year cycles | Exam in a mobile centre, three readings; mercury auscultatory through 2017–18, oscillometric from 2017–2020 | `BPQ020`: ever told by a doctor or health professional you had high blood pressure | Direct download from the CDC NHANES site, no registration |
| **KNHANES** (South Korea, KDCA) | All ages, annual | Health exam by trained staff, three readings | Physician-diagnosed hypertension item, plus treatment items | Free download after registering on the KNHANES site; English documentation available |
| **Health Survey for England** | Adults in private households, annual | Nurse visit, three oscillometric readings | Doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure item | UK Data Service: register, add to a project, accept the End User Licence; free |

If you want an ageing-cohort comparison instead, these three are designed as sister studies:

- **HRS (US, age 51+)**: blood pressure is measured by interviewers since 2006, on a rotating half of the sample each wave. Access is by free registration on the HRS site.
- **ELSA (England, 50+)**: blood pressure is measured in the nurse-visit waves only (2, 4, 6, and 8/9). Access is through the UK Data Service, as for HSE.
- **CHARLS (China, 45+)**: blood pressure was measured in 2011, 2013 and 2015. Access is by free registration and a short application on the CHARLS site.

The Gateway to Global Aging Data offers harmonized versions of all three, which saves recoding. SHARE (Europe) will not work, because its hypertension data are self-reported.

**NHANES details**
- **Files:** for each cycle, merge the demographics (`DEMO`), blood pressure questionnaire (`BPQ`) and exam files (`BPX`, or `BPXO` for oscillometric) on `SEQN`.
- **Weights:** use the exam weights (`WTMEC2YR`), not the interview weights, with `SDMVSTRA` and `SDMVPSU` for the design.
- **Cycles:** the 2019–March 2020 data were combined with 2017–18 into a "pre-pandemic" file with its own weight. The newest cycle is August 2021–August 2023.
- **Protocol change:** the switch from mercury to oscillometric devices affects trend comparisons. NCHS published a bridging study using 2017–18, when both methods were run.

**Things to settle in your methods**
- **Definition:** the usual one is mean measured blood pressure ≥140/90 (or ≥130/80) or current antihypertensive medication, with "unaware" meaning a "no" to the ever-told question. Use the same threshold and the same number of readings averaged across surveys.
- **Single-visit bias:** all of these surveys measure on one occasion, which overstates true hypertension and so overstates unawareness. This is a standard limitation to state.
- **Mode differences:** HSE nurse visits happen at home, while NHANES and KNHANES use exam centres. Nurse-visit subsamples also have their own weights.
- **Pandemic gaps:** HSE 2020 was cancelled and 2021 had reduced nurse coverage, so 2019 is the cleanest recent HSE year.

cases.name: ho-h-wrist-activity-outcomes
cases.promptMarkdown: I want to study whether physical activity and sleep patterns measured in daily life by wrist-worn accelerometers or activity trackers predict later disease and death. I need data from at least a few thousand adults who wore the device on the wrist for several days to a week or longer, linked to follow-up outcomes such as hospital records, diagnoses or death registrations. Wrist placement matters to me because I want my results to be comparable with other wrist-based studies. I'm at a US university and happy to go through applications. Which datasets should I consider, and what does getting access involve for each?

FAIL if the answer does not mention UK Biobank's accelerometer data, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

graders.name: 01-recall-ukbiobank-accelerometer
graders.evidence:
There are ten datasets worth considering, but only one (NHANES 2011–2014) is downloadable today, and the obvious first choice, UK Biobank, is reported closed to new applications right now. All facts below were checked on 12 November 2026 unless marked "from memory".

## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** device worn on the wrist for several days to a week or longer, in daily life.
- **R2 (must):** at least a few thousand adults.
- **R3 (must):** follow-up outcomes after the wear period, death at minimum.
- **R4 (nice):** disease outcomes from hospital records or diagnoses, not only death.
- **R5 (nice):** raw or high-resolution acceleration, since that is what makes wrist studies comparable. This is my assumption.
- **R6 (must):** obtainable by a US university researcher; applications and waiting are acceptable.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence / terms | Size (wrist data) | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES 2011–2014 + NCHS linked mortality | Direct download, minutes | US federal public-use data | 14,693 people, about 8,600 adults | Partial: death only | Today |
| 2 | All of Us (Fitbit + health records) | Institutional agreement; days if your university has one, otherwise weeks | Data Use and Registration Agreement; analysis only in the cloud Workbench | 68,000+ with Fitbit data | Strong, but consumer tracker | Today |
| 3 | UK Biobank accelerometer study | Application, fee, secure platform; new applications reported closed, so months | Material transfer agreement | 103,617 | Strong | Status from search results; official pages blocked |
| 4 | MrOS Sleep Study (older men) | Free account plus data use agreement, days | Data use agreement | about 3,050 | Partial: about 5 nights, old device | Today |
| 5 | Study of Osteoporotic Fractures (older women) | Free account plus data use agreement, days | Data use agreement | about 3,000 | Partial: about 4 nights | Today |
| 6 | Whitehall II (UK) | Application via Dementias Platform UK plus study committee, months | Data access agreement | 4,204 | Strong | Search summaries; page blocked |
| 7 | Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 | Collaboration request with University of Oulu, months | Study agreement | 5,481 | Partial: no raw data | Today |
| 8 | MESA Sleep (US) | Two applications (sleep data, then events), weeks | Data use agreements; commercial use tiered | 2,237 | Partial: linkage unconfirmed | Events page today; sleep-data page blocked |
| 9 | China Kadoorie Biobank resurvey | Application to access committee; timing unknown | Data access agreement | 21,897 | Partial: release unconfirmed | Paper today; access page blocked |
| 10 | CoLaus\|PsyCoLaus (Switzerland) | Proposal to study data centre, months | Data transfer agreement | about 2,600–2,700 | Partial | Today, from papers |

## Details

**1. NHANES 2011–2014 wrist accelerometry + public-use linked mortality** ([accelerometer file](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2011/DataFiles/PAXMIN_G.htm), [mortality files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/linked-data/mortality-files/))
- **Contents:** ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for 9 calendar days, in a US-representative sample, with minute, hour and day summaries. Raw 80 Hz files are also public (from memory).
- **Outcomes:** death only. Public-use mortality follow-up ends 31 December 2019, and cause of death may be perturbed for some records.
- **Access:** download both file sets and merge on the participant ID. Follow-up through 2022 and unaltered cause of death need a proposal to the NCHS Research Data Center (fee, weeks to months).
- **Extra:** derived minute-level step counts are on [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/minute-level-step-count-nhanes/1.0.2/) under CC0.
- **Limits:** death counts are modest (one paper reports 582 deaths among 3,032 adults aged 50+).
- **Used by:** [activity as the strongest mortality predictor](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11402588/); [diurnal activity and sleep patterns vs mortality](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12966-024-01673-9).

**2. All of Us Research Program** ([register](https://www.researchallofus.org/register/))
- **Contents:** Fitbit steps, heart rate and sleep, often over months or years, linked to health record diagnoses. Version 8 had 59,018 Fitbit participants, 36,614 of them with health records; version 9 has more than 68,000.
- **Access:** the page states "Only researchers whose institutions have signed a DURA may access the Researcher Workbench." Check the registered institutions list, then create an account, verify your identity, complete the training and sign the code of conduct.
- **Tiers:** the Registered Tier includes Fitbit and health record data with shifted dates. Cause of death needs the Controlled Tier.
- **Limits:** no raw acceleration; mostly participants' own devices, so a self-selected group; deaths come from health records and staff reports, and I found no National Death Index linkage. Data cannot leave the Workbench, and compute is billed.
- **Used by:** [step counts and chronic disease risk](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-022-02012-w); [the wearables dataset description](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04352-3).

**3. UK Biobank** ([accelerometer category](https://biobank.ndph.ox.ac.uk/showcase/label.cgi?id=1008), [apply](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/))
- **Contents:** Axivity AX3 on the wrist for 7 days (2013–2015) in 103,617 adults, linked to hospital, cancer and death records. This is the dataset other wrist studies compare against.
- **Current status:** search results quoting UK Biobank's own pages say all researcher access was shut on 23 April 2026 after exported data were found for sale. New applications remain closed, with a "late 2026" target and no confirmed date. I could not open the official pages myself.
- **Access when open:** free registration, project application (about 10 working days' review), institutional agreement, then analysis on its Research Analysis Platform with downloads blocked.
- **Fee:** £3,000 plus VAT for three years at the lowest tier, according to a third-party summary rather than UK Biobank's fees page.
- **Limits:** very heavily used, so simple activity–outcome questions are mostly published.
- **Used by:** [methods paper](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169649); [sleep regularity and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsad253); [activity and 697 incident diseases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-022-00676-9).

**4 and 5. MrOS and SOF** ([MrOS Online](https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/), [SOF Online](https://sofonline.ucsf.edu/))
- **Contents:** SleepWatch-O actigraph on the non-dominant wrist in about 3,050 men (mean age 76, 5.2 nights) and about 3,000 women (mean age 84, 4.1 nights).
- **Outcomes:** mortality (mean follow-up 12.1 and 5.4 years), plus adjudicated fractures and cardiovascular events (from memory).
- **Access:** both sites state "You must have an account and accept the terms of a Data Use Agreement before you can download or explore clinical data."
- **Limits:** old device with count-based output, short recordings and elderly single-sex cohorts.
- **Used by:** [rest-activity rhythms and mortality in MrOS](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20370475); [sleep duration phenotypes and mortality in both](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13698916).

**6. Whitehall II** ([data sharing page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/brain-sciences/psychiatry/research/mental-health-older-people/projects/whitehall-ii/data-sharing))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the non-dominant wrist for nine days in 2012–2013, 4,204 readable files, raw data at 85.7 Hz.
- **Outcomes:** mortality follow-up to August 2024 and incident dementia in published work.
- **Access:** apply through the Dementias Platform UK portal; its staff triage the request, then the Whitehall II data sharing committee reviews it.
- **To confirm:** whether raw files are released, and whether non-UK applicants are eligible.
- **Used by:** [sleep duration and dementia](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22354-2); [walking cadence and mortality](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13695056).

**7. Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966** ([programme page](https://www.oulu.fi/en/university/faculties-and-units/faculty-medicine/northern-finland-birth-cohorts-and-arctic-biobank))
- **Contents:** Polar Active on the non-dominant wrist for 14 days at age 46, 5,481 valid recordings.
- **Outcomes:** national hospital and death registers, with follow-up to the end of 2023.
- **Access:** data "can be requested for research collaboration projects with University of Oulu", so you need a local collaborator and a material request.
- **Limits:** single birth year, and the device gives activity levels, not raw acceleration.
- **Used by:** [sleep timing irregularity and cardiac events](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12872-026-05762-4).

**8. MESA Sleep** ([sleep data](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa), [events data](https://biolincc.nhlbi.nih.gov/studies/mesa/))
- **Contents:** Actiwatch Spectrum on the wrist for 7 days in 2,237 multi-ethnic US adults, as 30-second counts.
- **Outcomes:** held separately; the NHLBI repository offers "events data updated through calendar year 2020".
- **Access:** a data access agreement with the National Sleep Research Resource, plus a separate request to the NHLBI repository.
- **To confirm before applying:** whether the two releases share a participant identifier. Ask the MESA Coordinating Center.

**9. China Kadoorie Biobank** ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12966-023-01537-8))
- **Contents:** the same Axivity device and 7-day protocol as UK Biobank, in 21,897 adults in 2020–2021.
- **Access:** the paper says "Data are available upon reasonable request" and points to the biobank's data access page, which I could not open.
- **Limits:** whether the accelerometer data are released to outside researchers is unconfirmed, and follow-up since wear is short.

**10. CoLaus|PsyCoLaus** ([study site](https://www.colaus-psycolaus.ch/))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the right wrist for 14 days in about 2,600–2,700 adults, with a repeat measurement in 2018–2021.
- **Outcomes:** adjudicated cardiovascular events; I found no accelerometry–mortality paper.
- **Access:** e-mail a proposal to research.colaus@chuv.ch; the data are not posted publicly.
- **Used by:** [activity patterns and cardiovascular events](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11497381/).

## Known, not confirmed

- **UK Biobank status and fees:** from search summaries of its pages; the pages refused my tools. Check the apply page and researcher Community site.
- **Whitehall II and Dementias Platform UK steps:** both sites blocked automated reading; details are from search summaries and memory.
- **Sleep-data repository pages (MESA, MrOS, SOF):** my tools could not verify sleepdata.org's certificate; open it in a browser.
- **Seniors-ENRICA-2 (Spain), PREDIMED-Plus and MIPACT (Michigan, Apple Watch with health records):** recalled as possible fits; I found no access information.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Rush Memory and Aging Project:** wrist-worn with dementia and death outcomes, but analytic samples are about 700–1,000. The request site was unreachable today.
- **Rotterdam Study:** about 2,000 with mostly older wrist actigraphs; no release, only requests to the study management team.
- **NHANES 2003–2006, Tromsø7, German National Cohort:** hip-worn. Women's Health Study, WHI OPACH and REGARDS are also hip-worn (from memory).
- **HUNT4:** thigh and lower-back sensors.
- **BLSA, HANDLS, FinHealth 2017:** wrist-worn but under 1,000 participants each.

## What I could not find

- No openly downloadable dataset combines wrist accelerometry with hospital or diagnosis follow-up.
- Registry searches (OpenAIRE, Zenodo, DataCite, PhysioNet, Hugging Face) returned almost only small device-validation datasets; the cohorts above came from memory, the literature and project sites.

## Next step

1. Start on NHANES now to build your processing pipeline and mortality models.
2. Check whether your university is on the All of Us registered institutions list; if so, you can have diagnosis-linked data within days.
3. Watch for UK Biobank to reopen, and meanwhile send the Whitehall II application, the closest raw-data wrist cohort with long follow-up.
4. Before using any restricted dataset, check its agreement on third-party services, including online AI tools.

The interactive shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-PVHKEC/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- [UK Biobank Community FAQ: applying and accessing data](https://community.ukbiobank.ac.uk/hc/en-gb/articles/28002689502237-Applying-to-UK-Biobank-and-accessing-data-FAQ)

- [PublicTechnology: UK Biobank security review](https://www.publictechnology.net/2026/07/13/health-and-social-care/uk-biobank-commissions-200k-security-review-after-major-data-incident/)
- [All of Us: Curated Data Repository version 9](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/50653909888788-Our-Largest-Genomic-Dataset-Curated-Data-Repository-version-9)
- [All of Us: death data collection](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/10237876482196-How-to-find-participant-death-reports)
- [NCHS linked mortality files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/linked-data/mortality-files/)
- [MESA actigraphy introduction (sleepdata.org)](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa/pages/actigraphy-introduction.md)
- [China Kadoorie Biobank accelerometer paper](https://ijbnpa.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12966-023-01537-8)
- [NFBC1966 Polar Active dose-response paper](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6322295/)
- [Rush Memory and Aging Project overview](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3439198)
- [Rotterdam Study actigraphy and dementia](https://alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/alz.12122)

| 2 | All of Us (Fitbit + health records) | Institutional agreement; days if your university has one, otherwise weeks | Data Use and Registration Agreement; analysis only in the cloud Workbench | 68,000+ with Fitbit data | Strong, but consumer tracker | Today |

| 4 | MrOS Sleep Study (older men) | Free account plus data use agreement, days | Data use agreement | about 3,050 | Partial: about 5 nights, old device | Today |
| 5 | Study of Osteoporotic Fractures (older women) | Free account plus data use agreement, days | Data use agreement | about 3,000 | Partial: about 4 nights | Today |
| 6 | Whitehall II (UK) | Application via Dementias Platform UK plus study committee, months | Data access agreement | 4,204 | Strong | Search summaries; page blocked |
| 7 | Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 | Collaboration request with University of Oulu, months | Study agreement | 5,481 | Partial: no raw data | Today |
| 8 | MESA Sleep (US) | Two applications (sleep data, then events), weeks | Data use agreements; commercial use tiered | 2,237 | Partial: linkage unconfirmed | Events page today; sleep-data page blocked |
| 9 | China Kadoorie Biobank resurvey | Application to access committee; timing unknown | Data access agreement | 21,897 | Partial: release unconfirmed | Paper today; access page blocked |

- **Outcomes:** mortality (mean follow-up 12.1 and 5.4 years), plus adjudicated fractures and cardiovascular events (from memory).
- **Access:** both sites state "You must have an account and accept the terms of a Data Use Agreement before you can download or explore clinical data."
- **Limits:** old device with count-based output, short recordings and elderly single-sex cohorts.
- **Used by:** [rest-activity rhythms and mortality in MrOS](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20370475); [sleep duration phenotypes and mortality in both](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13698916).

- **Outcomes:** mortality follow-up to August 2024 and incident dementia in published work.

- **Limits:** whether the accelerometer data are released to outside researchers is unconfirmed, and follow-up since wear is short.

## Known, not confirmed

- **UK Biobank status and fees:** from search summaries of its pages; the pages refused my tools. Check the apply page and researcher Community site.
- **Whitehall II and Dementias Platform UK steps:** both sites blocked automated reading; details are from search summaries and memory.
- **Sleep-data repository pages (MESA, MrOS, SOF):** my tools could not verify sleepdata.org's certificate; open it in a browser.
- **Seniors-ENRICA-2 (Spain), PREDIMED-Plus and MIPACT (Michigan, Apple Watch with health records):** recalled as possible fits; I found no access information.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Rush Memory and Aging Project:** wrist-worn with dementia and death outcomes, but analytic samples are about 700–1,000. The request site was unreachable today.
- **Rotterdam Study:** about 2,000 with mostly older wrist actigraphs; no release, only requests to the study management team.
- **NHANES 2003–2006, Tromsø7, German National Cohort:** hip-worn. Women's Health Study, WHI OPACH and REGARDS are also hip-worn (from memory).
- **HUNT4:** thigh and lower-back sensors.
- **BLSA, HANDLS, FinHealth 2017:** wrist-worn but under 1,000 participants each.

## What I could not find

- No openly downloadable dataset combines wrist accelerometry with hospital or diagnosis follow-up.
- Registry searches (OpenAIRE, Zenodo, DataCite, PhysioNet, Hugging Face) returned almost only small device-validation datasets; the cohorts above came from memory, the literature and project sites.

## Next step

1. Start on NHANES now to build your processing pipeline and mortality models.
2. Check whether your university is on the All of Us registered institutions list; if so, you can have diagnosis-linked data within days.
3. Watch for UK Biobank to reopen, and meanwhile send the Whitehall II application, the closest raw-data wrist cohort with long follow-up.
4. Before using any restricted dataset, check its agreement on third-party services, including online AI tools.

- **Access:** the page states "Only researchers whose institutions have signed a DURA may access the Researcher Workbench." Check the registered institutions list, then create an account, verify your identity, complete the training and sign the code of conduct.
- **Tiers:** the Registered Tier includes Fitbit and health record data with shifted dates. Cause of death needs the Controlled Tier.
- **Limits:** no raw acceleration; mostly participants' own devices, so a self-selected group; deaths come from health records and staff reports, and I found no National Death Index linkage. Data cannot leave the Workbench, and compute is billed.
- **Used by:** [step counts and chronic disease risk](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-022-02012-w); [the wearables dataset description](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04352-3).

**3. UK Biobank** ([accelerometer category](https://biobank.ndph.ox.ac.uk/showcase/label.cgi?id=1008), [apply](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/))
- **Contents:** Axivity AX3 on the wrist for 7 days (2013–2015) in 103,617 adults, linked to hospital, cancer and death records. This is the dataset other wrist studies compare against.
- **Current status:** search results quoting UK Biobank's own pages say all researcher access was shut on 23 April 2026 after exported data were found for sale. New applications remain closed, with a "late 2026" target and no confirmed date. I could not open the official pages myself.
- **Access when open:** free registration, project application (about 10 working days' review), institutional agreement, then analysis on its Research Analysis Platform with downloads blocked.
- **Fee:** £3,000 plus VAT for three years at the lowest tier, according to a third-party summary rather than UK Biobank's fees page.
- **Limits:** very heavily used, so simple activity–outcome questions are mostly published.
- **Used by:** [methods paper](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169649); [sleep regularity and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsad253); [activity and 697 incident diseases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-022-00676-9).

**4 and 5. MrOS and SOF** ([MrOS Online](https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/), [SOF Online](https://sofonline.ucsf.edu/))
- **Contents:** SleepWatch-O actigraph on the non-dominant wrist in about 3,050 men (mean age 76, 5.2 nights) and about 3,000 women (mean age 84, 4.1 nights).
- **Outcomes:** mortality (mean follow-up 12.1 and 5.4 years), plus adjudicated fractures and cardiovascular events (from memory).
- **Access:** both sites state "You must have an account and accept the terms of a Data Use Agreement before you can download or explore clinical data."
- **Limits:** old device with count-based output, short recordings and elderly single-sex cohorts.
- **Used by:** [rest-activity rhythms and mortality in MrOS](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20370475); [sleep duration phenotypes and mortality in both](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13698916).

**6. Whitehall II** ([data sharing page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/brain-sciences/psychiatry/research/mental-health-older-people/projects/whitehall-ii/data-sharing))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the non-dominant wrist for nine days in 2012–2013, 4,204 readable files, raw data at 85.7 Hz.
- **Outcomes:** mortality follow-up to August 2024 and incident dementia in published work.
- **Access:** apply through the Dementias Platform UK portal; its staff triage the request, then the Whitehall II data sharing committee reviews it.
- **To confirm:** whether raw files are released, and whether non-UK applicants are eligible.
- **Used by:** [sleep duration and dementia](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22354-2); [walking cadence and mortality](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13695056).

**7. Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966** ([programme page](https://www.oulu.fi/en/university/faculties-and-units/faculty-medicine/northern-finland-birth-cohorts-and-arctic-biobank))
- **Contents:** Polar Active on the non-dominant wrist for 14 days at age 46, 5,481 valid recordings.
- **Outcomes:** national hospital and death registers, with follow-up to the end of 2023.
- **Access:** data "can be requested for research collaboration projects with University of Oulu", so you need a local collaborator and a material request.
- **Limits:** single birth year, and the device gives activity levels, not raw acceleration.
- **Used by:** [sleep timing irregularity and cardiac events](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12872-026-05762-4).

**8. MESA Sleep** ([sleep data](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa), [events data](https://biolincc.nhlbi.nih.gov/studies/mesa/))
- **Contents:** Actiwatch Spectrum on the wrist for 7 days in 2,237 multi-ethnic US adults, as 30-second counts.
- **Outcomes:** held separately; the NHLBI repository offers "events data updated through calendar year 2020".
- **Access:** a data access agreement with the National Sleep Research Resource, plus a separate request to the NHLBI repository.
- **To confirm before applying:** whether the two releases share a participant identifier. Ask the MESA Coordinating Center.

**9. China Kadoorie Biobank** ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12966-023-01537-8))
- **Contents:** the same Axivity device and 7-day protocol as UK Biobank, in 21,897 adults in 2020–2021.
- **Access:** the paper says "Data are available upon reasonable request" and points to the biobank's data access page, which I could not open.
- **Limits:** whether the accelerometer data are released to outside researchers is unconfirmed, and follow-up since wear is short.

**10. CoLaus|PsyCoLaus** ([study site](https://www.colaus-psycolaus.ch/))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the right wrist for 14 days in about 2,600–2,700 adults, with a repeat measurement in 2018–2021.
- **Outcomes:** adjudicated cardiovascular events; I found no accelerometry–mortality paper.
- **Access:** e-mail a proposal to research.colaus@chuv.ch; the data are not posted publicly.
- **Used by:** [activity patterns and cardiovascular events](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11497381/).

## Known, not confirmed

- **UK Biobank status and fees:** from search summaries of its pages; the pages refused my tools. Check the apply page and researcher Community site.
- **Whitehall II and Dementias Platform UK steps:** both sites blocked automated reading; details are from search summaries and memory.
- **Sleep-data repository pages (MESA, MrOS, SOF):** my tools could not verify sleepdata.org's certificate; open it in a browser.
- **Seniors-ENRICA-2 (Spain), PREDIMED-Plus and MIPACT (Michigan, Apple Watch with health records):** recalled as possible fits; I found no access information.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Rush Memory and Aging Project:** wrist-worn with dementia and death outcomes, but analytic samples are about 700–1,000. The request site was unreachable today.
- **Rotterdam Study:** about 2,000 with mostly older wrist actigraphs; no release, only requests to the study management team.
- **NHANES 2003–2006, Tromsø7, German National Cohort:** hip-worn. Women's Health Study, WHI OPACH and REGARDS are also hip-worn (from memory).
- **HUNT4:** thigh and lower-back sensors.
- **BLSA, HANDLS, FinHealth 2017:** wrist-worn but under 1,000 participants each.

## What I could not find

- No openly downloadable dataset combines wrist accelerometry with hospital or diagnosis follow-up.
- Registry searches (OpenAIRE, Zenodo, DataCite, PhysioNet, Hugging Face) returned almost only small device-validation datasets; the cohorts above came from memory, the literature and project sites.

## Next step

1. Start on NHANES now to build your processing pipeline and mortality models.
2. Check whether your university is on the All of Us registered institutions list; if so, you can have diagnosis-linked data within days.
3. Watch for UK Biobank to reopen, and meanwhile send the Whitehall II application, the closest raw-data wrist cohort with long follow-up.
4. Before using any restricted dataset, check its agreement on third-party services, including online AI tools.

The interactive shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-PVHKEC/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-ukbiobank-accelerometer
graders.evidence:
Six datasets fit, but the best-known one, UK Biobank, appears to have paused new applications since April 2026, so NHANES (open today) and All of Us (days, if your university has an agreement in place) are where to start. I could not open the official UK Biobank, All of Us, Whitehall II or NSRR pages directly (they block automated readers), so their access terms below come from search results and memory, as marked.

## What I assumed you need

- **Wrist placement (must):** a research accelerometer or consumer tracker worn on the wrist.
- **Wear time (must):** free-living wear for several days to a week or longer.
- **Size (must):** at least a few thousand adults.
- **Outcomes (must):** linked deaths, hospital records or diagnoses after the wear period.
- **Access (must):** obtainable from a US university; applications are fine.
- **Activity and sleep (nice to have):** 24-hour wear with minute-level or raw data, so both can be derived.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES 2011–2014 wrist accelerometry + public linked mortality files | Open download, minutes | No formal licence; NCHS data-use terms | 14,693 wearers of all ages; about 7,100 adults in a 2026 mortality paper | Strong, but deaths only | Today |
| 2 | All of Us Fitbit + health records | Institutional agreement, then individual registration and training; days if the agreement exists; cloud-only analysis | Data User Code of Conduct | More than 59,000 with wearable data | Strong, but consumer device with no raw signal | Search results today; official site not read |
| 3 | UK Biobank accelerometer sub-study | Application, institutional agreement and fee; new applications reported paused; months | Material Transfer Agreement | About 100,000 | Strongest on content | Search results today; official site not read |
| 4 | Whitehall II accelerometer sub-study | Application to the study's data sharing committee plus signed agreement; months | Study access agreement | About 4,000 | Strong | Search results today; official site not read |
| 5 | MrOS and SOF wrist actigraphy | Free account plus click-through data use agreement; days | Data Use Agreement | About 3,000 men and 3,000 women | Partial | Today (home pages) |
| 6 | MESA Sleep actigraphy | NSRR request plus a separate BioLINCC application for outcomes; weeks | Per-dataset agreements | 2,237 | Partial | Search results and memory |

## Details

**1. NHANES 2011–2014** ([accelerometer documentation](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2011/DataFiles/PAXMIN_G.htm), [linked mortality files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/linked-data/mortality-files/))
- **Contents:** ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for seven 24-hour days, in a US national sample. Minute-level and raw 80 Hz files are public, with an algorithm-predicted wake/sleep/non-wear flag.
- **Outcomes:** deaths only, through 31 December 2019. The public mortality files replace follow-up time or cause of death with synthetic values for some records; vital status is unaltered.
- **What is missing:** no public hospital or diagnosis linkage. Unaltered mortality data need an approved project at the NCHS Research Data Center; Medicare and Medicaid linkage sits there too (from memory).
- **Steps:** download the accelerometer files for both cycles, download the mortality files, merge on the participant ID.
- **Shortcut:** an open [PhysioNet release](https://physionet.org/content/minute-level-step-count-nhanes/1.0.2/) (CC0) provides minute-level step counts already derived from the raw data.
- **Used by:** [activity fragmentation and cause-specific mortality, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-29778-9).

**2. All of Us** ([CDR v8 release notes](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/30294451486356-Curated-Data-Repository-CDR-version-8-Release-Notes), [NIH research page](https://www.nih.gov/allofus/research))
- **Contents:** Fitbit steps, heart rate, activity and sleep stages, often over months or years, linked to health record diagnoses. Wearable data are in the Registered Tier.
- **What is missing:** no raw acceleration, and metrics come from Fitbit's proprietary algorithms. Device model is recorded for about 90% of donors, so filter to wrist models. Death capture is incomplete (from memory).
- **Steps:**
  1. Confirm your university has signed the Data Use and Registration Agreement.
  2. Register with identity verification.
  3. Complete the responsible conduct training and sign the code of conduct.
  4. Create a workspace with a public project description.
- **Conditions:** analysis happens only inside the cloud Workbench, with no participant-level downloads. Compute is billed after initial credits (from memory).
- **Used by:** [sleep patterns and chronic disease](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-03155-8), [11 million days of Fitbit data](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78529-2), [activity and chronic disease risk](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-025-01372-x).

**3. UK Biobank** ([apply for access](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/))
- **Contents:** Axivity AX3 wrist accelerometer for seven days in 2013–2015, with raw data, linked to hospital records and to cancer and death registries. This is the cohort most wrist studies compare against.
- **Current status:** search results say the analysis platform was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data were found for sale. New project applications were still paused as of late October, with a "late 2026" target and no confirmed date. Confirm this on the official page before planning.
- **Steps when open:** register in the Access Management System, submit a project application, have your institution sign the transfer agreement, and pay the fee.
- **Fees:** search results cite £3,000 to £9,000 plus VAT for three years depending on tier, with a reduced student rate. I did not confirm which tier covers accelerometry.
- **Timing:** about 15 weeks was quoted for normal times. Analysis is on the cloud platform only.
- **Interim route:** ask whether a colleague already holds an approved project you could join. I could not confirm that additions are being processed during the pause.
- **Used by:** [the methods paper](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169649), [sleep regularity and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsad253), [step counts and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1249/mss.0000000000003478).

**4. Whitehall II** ([data sharing page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/brain-sciences/psychiatry/our-research/mental-health-older-people/whitehall-ii/data-sharing))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the non-dominant wrist for nine days in 2012–2013, with 4,008 valid recordings in adults aged 60–83. Deaths come from the NHS register (633 deaths, followed to November 2023 in a 2025 paper), and diagnoses from hospital records.
- **What is missing:** it is an occupational cohort that is about three-quarters men. I could not confirm whether raw accelerometer files and linked hospital data are released to external applicants on the same terms as the core data.
- **Steps:** apply directly to the study team or through the Dementias Platform UK portal. The platform triages, the Whitehall II committee decides, and you sign the access agreement.
- **Used by:** [Whitehall II and UK Biobank mortality comparison](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-30237-5), which is a ready template for cross-cohort comparability, and [activity and successful ageing](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep45772).

**5. MrOS and SOF** ([MrOS Online](https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/), [SOF Online](https://sofonline.ucsf.edu/))
- **Contents:** wrist actigraphy in older US men (about 5 days, 2003–2005) and older women, with long study-adjudicated follow-up for death, fractures and cardiovascular events.
- **What is missing:** these are count-based actigraphs from the early 2000s, so intensity metrics will not map onto modern raw-acceleration measures. I could not confirm whether epoch-level files are downloadable or what actigraphy SOF Online holds.
- **Steps:** register on each site and accept the data use agreement. Both home pages state: "You must have an account and accept the terms of a Data Use Agreement before you can download or explore clinical data."
- **Used by:** [rest-activity rhythms and mortality in MrOS](https://doi.org/10.3109/07420520903419157), [incident diabetes](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc20-0557), [SOF and MrOS combined](https://doi.org/10.1093/geroni/igy023.363).

**6. MESA Sleep** ([NSRR page](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa))
- **Contents:** Actiwatch Spectrum on the wrist for seven days in 2010–2013, in a multi-ethnic US cohort; 2,159 people have epoch files.
- **What is missing:** cardiovascular events and deaths are not on NSRR. They need a separate BioLINCC application with an ethics determination and an institution-signed agreement (from memory).
- **Steps:** request the actigraphy from NSRR, apply to BioLINCC for the events data, and merge on the BioLINCC participant ID.

## Known, not confirmed

- **China Kadoorie Biobank, third resurvey:** about 20,000 adults wore an Axivity AX3 on the wrist for seven days in 2020–2021 ([description paper](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12966-023-01537-8)). The open-access policy I found covers baseline, the first two resurveys and disease follow-up, not this resurvey. Check the [data access page](https://www.ckbiobank.org/data-access) for the release schedule; collaboration with the study team may be the only route.
- **Rotterdam Study:** wrist actigraphy with mortality follow-up in 1,734 people ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwu245)). From memory, data go by request to the study's management team and export is restricted. I did not confirm the procedure or any later, larger wave.
- **CoLaus|PsyCoLaus (Lausanne):** from memory, about 2,900 adults with 14 days of wrist GENEActiv. It was used as the external validation cohort for a Whitehall II mortality model. Access is by request to the study's committee, not confirmed.

## Not recommended, and why

- **NHANES 2003–2006:** open with long mortality follow-up, but the device was hip-worn.
- **German National Cohort (NAKO):** hip-worn, and applications were described as limited to researchers in EU countries.
- **WHI OPACH, Women's Health Study, REGARDS:** large US cohorts with outcomes, but hip-worn (from memory).
- **HCHS/SOL Sueño:** wrist actigraphy for a week, but only 1,887 people in the public epoch files and I found no outcome linkage.
- **CAPTURE-24 and similar activity-recognition sets:** open raw wrist data, but about 150 people and no outcomes.

## What I could not find

- No dataset accessible now pairs raw wrist accelerometry with hospital-record linkage at UK Biobank scale. NHANES has deaths only in its public files; All of Us has diagnoses but no raw signal.
- Registry searches returned almost only paper supplements and unrelated datasets; everything above came from the literature and study portals.

## Next step

Download NHANES today and build your pipeline on it. In parallel, ask your research office whether the All of Us agreement is signed, and send the Whitehall II application, since it is the slowest. Check the UK Biobank application page for a reopening date, and ask your institution early whether these secondary analyses need an ethics exemption.

The interactive shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-JDr6IM/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`. Checked 12 November 2026.

Sources not linked above:
- [UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/research-analysis-platform/)
- [UK Biobank community FAQ: Can I apply to use UK Biobank data?](https://community.ukbiobank.ac.uk/hc/en-gb/articles/37284734505117-Can-I-apply-to-use-UK-Biobank-data)
- [UK Biobank Oversight Committee report, June 2026](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/UK-Biobank-Oversight-Committee-report-June-2026.pdf)
- [All of Us Data Access Framework](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/22346942074132-Data-Access-Framework)
- [The All of Us wearables dataset, Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04352-3)
- [Dementias Platform UK cohort data availability](https://portal.dementiasplatform.uk/data/cohort-data-availability/)
- [Movement-behaviour profiles and mortality in Whitehall II](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11216065/)
- [NSRR MrOS page](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mros)
- [NSRR MESA actigraphy introduction](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa/pages/actigraphy-introduction.md)
- [NSRR HCHS/SOL actigraphy introduction](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/hchs/pages/actigraphy-introduction.md)
- [China Kadoorie Biobank third resurvey news item](https://www.ckbiobank.org/news-1/3rd-resurvey-of-ckb-participants-completed)
- [Pooled UK Biobank and NAKO accelerometer analysis](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12966-026-01980-3)

- **Fees:** search results cite £3,000 to £9,000 plus VAT for three years depending on tier, with a reduced student rate. I did not confirm which tier covers accelerometry.

- **Interim route:** ask whether a colleague already holds an approved project you could join. I could not confirm that additions are being processed during the pause.

Six datasets fit, but the best-known one, UK Biobank, appears to have paused new applications since April 2026, so NHANES (open today) and All of Us (days, if your university has an agreement in place) are where to start. I could not open the official UK Biobank, All of Us, Whitehall II or NSRR pages directly (they block automated readers), so their access terms below come from search results and memory, as marked.

## What I assumed you need

- **Wrist placement (must):** a research accelerometer or consumer tracker worn on the wrist.
- **Wear time (must):** free-living wear for several days to a week or longer.
- **Size (must):** at least a few thousand adults.
- **Outcomes (must):** linked deaths, hospital records or diagnoses after the wear period.
- **Access (must):** obtainable from a US university; applications are fine.
- **Activity and sleep (nice to have):** 24-hour wear with minute-level or raw data, so both can be derived.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES 2011–2014 wrist accelerometry + public linked mortality files | Open download, minutes | No formal licence; NCHS data-use terms | 14,693 wearers of all ages; about 7,100 adults in a 2026 mortality paper | Strong, but deaths only | Today |
| 2 | All of Us Fitbit + health records | Institutional agreement, then individual registration and training; days if the agreement exists; cloud-only analysis | Data User Code of Conduct | More than 59,000 with wearable data | Strong, but consumer device with no raw signal | Search results today; official site not read |
| 3 | UK Biobank accelerometer sub-study | Application, institutional agreement and fee; new applications reported paused; months | Material Transfer Agreement | About 100,000 | Strongest on content | Search results today; official site not read |
| 4 | Whitehall II accelerometer sub-study | Application to the study's data sharing committee plus signed agreement; months | Study access agreement | About 4,000 | Strong | Search results today; official site not read |
| 5 | MrOS and SOF wrist actigraphy | Free account plus click-through data use agreement; days | Data Use Agreement | About 3,000 men and 3,000 women | Partial | Today (home pages) |
| 6 | MESA Sleep actigraphy | NSRR request plus a separate BioLINCC application for outcomes; weeks | Per-dataset agreements | 2,237 | Partial | Search results and memory |

**1. NHANES 2011–2014** ([accelerometer documentation](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2011/DataFiles/PAXMIN_G.htm), [linked mortality files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/linked-data/mortality-files/))

- **Shortcut:** an open [PhysioNet release](https://physionet.org/content/minute-level-step-count-nhanes/1.0.2/) (CC0) provides minute-level step counts already derived from the raw data.
- **Used by:** [activity fragmentation and cause-specific mortality, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-29778-9).

**2. All of Us** ([CDR v8 release notes](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/30294451486356-Curated-Data-Repository-CDR-version-8-Release-Notes), [NIH research page](https://www.nih.gov/allofus/research))
- **Contents:** Fitbit steps, heart rate, activity and sleep stages, often over months or years, linked to health record diagnoses. Wearable data are in the Registered Tier.
- **What is missing:** no raw acceleration, and metrics come from Fitbit's proprietary algorithms. Device model is recorded for about 90% of donors, so filter to wrist models. Death capture is incomplete (from memory).
- **Steps:**
  1. Confirm your university has signed the Data Use and Registration Agreement.
  2. Register with identity verification.
  3. Complete the responsible conduct training and sign the code of conduct.
  4. Create a workspace with a public project description.
- **Conditions:** analysis happens only inside the cloud Workbench, with no participant-level downloads. Compute is billed after initial credits (from memory).
- **Used by:** [sleep patterns and chronic disease](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-03155-8), [11 million days of Fitbit data](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78529-2), [activity and chronic disease risk](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-025-01372-x).

**3. UK Biobank** ([apply for access](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/))
- **Contents:** Axivity AX3 wrist accelerometer for seven days in 2013–2015, with raw data, linked to hospital records and to cancer and death registries. This is the cohort most wrist studies compare against.
- **Current status:** search results say the analysis platform was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data were found for sale. New project applications were still paused as of late October, with a "late 2026" target and no confirmed date. Confirm this on the official page before planning.
- **Steps when open:** register in the Access Management System, submit a project application, have your institution sign the transfer agreement, and pay the fee.
- **Fees:** search results cite £3,000 to £9,000 plus VAT for three years depending on tier, with a reduced student rate. I did not confirm which tier covers accelerometry.
- **Timing:** about 15 weeks was quoted for normal times. Analysis is on the cloud platform only.
- **Interim route:** ask whether a colleague already holds an approved project you could join. I could not confirm that additions are being processed during the pause.
- **Used by:** [the methods paper](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169649), [sleep regularity and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsad253), [step counts and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1249/mss.0000000000003478).

**4. Whitehall II** ([data sharing page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/brain-sciences/psychiatry/our-research/mental-health-older-people/whitehall-ii/data-sharing))

- **What is missing:** it is an occupational cohort that is about three-quarters men. I could not confirm whether raw accelerometer files and linked hospital data are released to external applicants on the same terms as the core data.
- **Steps:** apply directly to the study team or through the Dementias Platform UK portal. The platform triages, the Whitehall II committee decides, and you sign the access agreement.
- **Used by:** [Whitehall II and UK Biobank mortality comparison](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-30237-5), which is a ready template for cross-cohort comparability, and [activity and successful ageing](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep45772).

graders.name: 07-trap-nhanes-hip
graders.evidence:
Six datasets fit, but the best-known one, UK Biobank, appears to have paused new applications since April 2026, so NHANES (open today) and All of Us (days, if your university has an agreement in place) are where to start. I could not open the official UK Biobank, All of Us, Whitehall II or NSRR pages directly (they block automated readers), so their access terms below come from search results and memory, as marked.

## What I assumed you need

- **Wrist placement (must):** a research accelerometer or consumer tracker worn on the wrist.
- **Wear time (must):** free-living wear for several days to a week or longer.
- **Size (must):** at least a few thousand adults.
- **Outcomes (must):** linked deaths, hospital records or diagnoses after the wear period.
- **Access (must):** obtainable from a US university; applications are fine.
- **Activity and sleep (nice to have):** 24-hour wear with minute-level or raw data, so both can be derived.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES 2011–2014 wrist accelerometry + public linked mortality files | Open download, minutes | No formal licence; NCHS data-use terms | 14,693 wearers of all ages; about 7,100 adults in a 2026 mortality paper | Strong, but deaths only | Today |
| 2 | All of Us Fitbit + health records | Institutional agreement, then individual registration and training; days if the agreement exists; cloud-only analysis | Data User Code of Conduct | More than 59,000 with wearable data | Strong, but consumer device with no raw signal | Search results today; official site not read |
| 3 | UK Biobank accelerometer sub-study | Application, institutional agreement and fee; new applications reported paused; months | Material Transfer Agreement | About 100,000 | Strongest on content | Search results today; official site not read |
| 4 | Whitehall II accelerometer sub-study | Application to the study's data sharing committee plus signed agreement; months | Study access agreement | About 4,000 | Strong | Search results today; official site not read |
| 5 | MrOS and SOF wrist actigraphy | Free account plus click-through data use agreement; days | Data Use Agreement | About 3,000 men and 3,000 women | Partial | Today (home pages) |
| 6 | MESA Sleep actigraphy | NSRR request plus a separate BioLINCC application for outcomes; weeks | Per-dataset agreements | 2,237 | Partial | Search results and memory |

## Details

**1. NHANES 2011–2014** ([accelerometer documentation](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2011/DataFiles/PAXMIN_G.htm), [linked mortality files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/linked-data/mortality-files/))
- **Contents:** ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for seven 24-hour days, in a US national sample. Minute-level and raw 80 Hz files are public, with an algorithm-predicted wake/sleep/non-wear flag.
- **Outcomes:** deaths only, through 31 December 2019. The public mortality files replace follow-up time or cause of death with synthetic values for some records; vital status is unaltered.
- **What is missing:** no public hospital or diagnosis linkage. Unaltered mortality data need an approved project at the NCHS Research Data Center; Medicare and Medicaid linkage sits there too (from memory).
- **Steps:** download the accelerometer files for both cycles, download the mortality files, merge on the participant ID.
- **Shortcut:** an open [PhysioNet release](https://physionet.org/content/minute-level-step-count-nhanes/1.0.2/) (CC0) provides minute-level step counts already derived from the raw data.
- **Used by:** [activity fragmentation and cause-specific mortality, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-29778-9).

**2. All of Us** ([CDR v8 release notes](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/30294451486356-Curated-Data-Repository-CDR-version-8-Release-Notes), [NIH research page](https://www.nih.gov/allofus/research))
- **Contents:** Fitbit steps, heart rate, activity and sleep stages, often over months or years, linked to health record diagnoses. Wearable data are in the Registered Tier.
- **What is missing:** no raw acceleration, and metrics come from Fitbit's proprietary algorithms. Device model is recorded for about 90% of donors, so filter to wrist models. Death capture is incomplete (from memory).
- **Steps:**
  1. Confirm your university has signed the Data Use and Registration Agreement.
  2. Register with identity verification.
  3. Complete the responsible conduct training and sign the code of conduct.
  4. Create a workspace with a public project description.
- **Conditions:** analysis happens only inside the cloud Workbench, with no participant-level downloads. Compute is billed after initial credits (from memory).
- **Used by:** [sleep patterns and chronic disease](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-03155-8), [11 million days of Fitbit data](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78529-2), [activity and chronic disease risk](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-025-01372-x).

**3. UK Biobank** ([apply for access](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/))
- **Contents:** Axivity AX3 wrist accelerometer for seven days in 2013–2015, with raw data, linked to hospital records and to cancer and death registries. This is the cohort most wrist studies compare against.
- **Current status:** search results say the analysis platform was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data were found for sale. New project applications were still paused as of late October, with a "late 2026" target and no confirmed date. Confirm this on the official page before planning.
- **Steps when open:** register in the Access Management System, submit a project application, have your institution sign the transfer agreement, and pay the fee.
- **Fees:** search results cite £3,000 to £9,000 plus VAT for three years depending on tier, with a reduced student rate. I did not confirm which tier covers accelerometry.
- **Timing:** about 15 weeks was quoted for normal times. Analysis is on the cloud platform only.
- **Interim route:** ask whether a colleague already holds an approved project you could join. I could not confirm that additions are being processed during the pause.
- **Used by:** [the methods paper](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169649), [sleep regularity and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsad253), [step counts and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1249/mss.0000000000003478).

**4. Whitehall II** ([data sharing page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/brain-sciences/psychiatry/our-research/mental-health-older-people/whitehall-ii/data-sharing))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the non-dominant wrist for nine days in 2012–2013, with 4,008 valid recordings in adults aged 60–83. Deaths come from the NHS register (633 deaths, followed to November 2023 in a 2025 paper), and diagnoses from hospital records.
- **What is missing:** it is an occupational cohort that is about three-quarters men. I could not confirm whether raw accelerometer files and linked hospital data are released to external applicants on the same terms as the core data.
- **Steps:** apply directly to the study team or through the Dementias Platform UK portal. The platform triages, the Whitehall II committee decides, and you sign the access agreement.
- **Used by:** [Whitehall II and UK Biobank mortality comparison](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-30237-5), which is a ready template for cross-cohort comparability, and [activity and successful ageing](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep45772).

**5. MrOS and SOF** ([MrOS Online](https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/), [SOF Online](https://sofonline.ucsf.edu/))
- **Contents:** wrist actigraphy in older US men (about 5 days, 2003–2005) and older women, with long study-adjudicated follow-up for death, fractures and cardiovascular events.
- **What is missing:** these are count-based actigraphs from the early 2000s, so intensity metrics will not map onto modern raw-acceleration measures. I could not confirm whether epoch-level files are downloadable or what actigraphy SOF Online holds.
- **Steps:** register on each site and accept the data use agreement. Both home pages state: "You must have an account and accept the terms of a Data Use Agreement before you can download or explore clinical data."
- **Used by:** [rest-activity rhythms and mortality in MrOS](https://doi.org/10.3109/07420520903419157), [incident diabetes](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc20-0557), [SOF and MrOS combined](https://doi.org/10.1093/geroni/igy023.363).

**6. MESA Sleep** ([NSRR page](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa))
- **Contents:** Actiwatch Spectrum on the wrist for seven days in 2010–2013, in a multi-ethnic US cohort; 2,159 people have epoch files.
- **What is missing:** cardiovascular events and deaths are not on NSRR. They need a separate BioLINCC application with an ethics determination and an institution-signed agreement (from memory).
- **Steps:** request the actigraphy from NSRR, apply to BioLINCC for the events data, and merge on the BioLINCC participant ID.

## Known, not confirmed

- **China Kadoorie Biobank, third resurvey:** about 20,000 adults wore an Axivity AX3 on the wrist for seven days in 2020–2021 ([description paper](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12966-023-01537-8)). The open-access policy I found covers baseline, the first two resurveys and disease follow-up, not this resurvey. Check the [data access page](https://www.ckbiobank.org/data-access) for the release schedule; collaboration with the study team may be the only route.
- **Rotterdam Study:** wrist actigraphy with mortality follow-up in 1,734 people ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwu245)). From memory, data go by request to the study's management team and export is restricted. I did not confirm the procedure or any later, larger wave.
- **CoLaus|PsyCoLaus (Lausanne):** from memory, about 2,900 adults with 14 days of wrist GENEActiv. It was used as the external validation cohort for a Whitehall II mortality model. Access is by request to the study's committee, not confirmed.

## Not recommended, and why

- **NHANES 2003–2006:** open with long mortality follow-up, but the device was hip-worn.
- **German National Cohort (NAKO):** hip-worn, and applications were described as limited to researchers in EU countries.
- **WHI OPACH, Women's Health Study, REGARDS:** large US cohorts with outcomes, but hip-worn (from memory).
- **HCHS/SOL Sueño:** wrist actigraphy for a week, but only 1,887 people in the public epoch files and I found no outcome linkage.
- **CAPTURE-24 and similar activity-recognition sets:** open raw wrist data, but about 150 people and no outcomes.

## What I could not find

- No dataset accessible now pairs raw wrist accelerometry with hospital-record linkage at UK Biobank scale. NHANES has deaths only in its public files; All of Us has diagnoses but no raw signal.
- Registry searches returned almost only paper supplements and unrelated datasets; everything above came from the literature and study portals.

## Next step

Download NHANES today and build your pipeline on it. In parallel, ask your research office whether the All of Us agreement is signed, and send the Whitehall II application, since it is the slowest. Check the UK Biobank application page for a reopening date, and ask your institution early whether these secondary analyses need an ethics exemption.

The interactive shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-JDr6IM/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`. Checked 12 November 2026.

graders.name: 01-recall-ukbiobank-accelerometer
graders.evidence:
For your design, three datasets do most of the work: NHANES 2011–2014 (usable today), UK Biobank (the field's reference dataset, but access is suspended right now), and All of Us (the only large tracker-based option). I checked access terms on the web today; items marked "from memory" I did not re-verify.

## Main options

| Dataset | Wrist device and wear | Size | Linked outcomes | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NHANES 2011–2014** | ActiGraph GT3X+, non-dominant wrist, 7 days, 24 h | About 7,600 adults with valid wear | Deaths via National Death Index through 31 Dec 2019 | Public download, no application |
| **UK Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days (2013–15) | About 100,000 adults (from memory) | Hospital records, cancer and death registries | Paid application; currently on hold |
| **All of Us** | Participants' Fitbits, often months to years | About 59,000 with Fitbit data; roughly 22,000–29,000 also have health records | Electronic health records; deaths only from those records | Institutional agreement, free |
| **Whitehall II** | GENEActiv, non-dominant wrist, 9 days (2012–13) | About 4,200, aged 60–83 | NHS mortality register through 2024; hospital records | Application to UCL |
| **China Kadoorie Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days (2020–21) | About 20,000–21,000 | Death and hospitalisation records (from memory) | Application; release status unconfirmed |

## What access involves

- **NHANES:** Download the minute-level files (PAXMIN) and the public-use linked mortality file from CDC.
  - The public mortality file has perturbed follow-up values for some records and limited cause-of-death detail.
  - Full mortality detail and Medicare/Medicaid linkage need a proposal to the NCHS Research Data Center, with fees and on-site or remote enclave analysis (from memory).
- **UK Biobank:** Normally you register, submit a project application, have your institution sign a Material Transfer Agreement, and pay.
  - Fees are £3,000 for three years at Tier 1, plus VAT and cloud compute; analysis runs only on their cloud platform. I could not confirm which tier covers the accelerometer data.
  - Access was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data appeared for sale. New applications are on hold, with "late 2026" targeted for reopening and no firm date.
  - Approval took about 15 weeks on average before the suspension.
